title.zh: 卷一百九十 列傳第七十八 楊廷和 梁儲 蔣冕 毛紀 石九珤
title.en: Volume 190 Biographies 78: Yang Tinghe, Liang Chu, Jiang Mian, Mao Ji, Shi Jiubao
title.raw: 卷一百九十 列傳第七十八 楊廷和 梁儲 蔣冕 毛紀 石九珤 Volume 190 Biographies 78: Yang Tinghe, Liang Chu, Jiang Mian, Mao Ji, Shi Jiubao

sentences.zh: 楊廷和梁儲蔣冕毛紀石缶

translations.literal: Yang Tinghe, Liang Chu, Jiang Mian, Mao Ji, and Shi Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tinghe, Liang Chu, Jiang Mian, Mao Ji, and Shi Jiubao.

sentences.zh: （兄玠）〉

translations.literal: (elder brother Jie) — closing subsection bracket 〉.〉
translations.idiomatic: (elder brother Jie))〉

sentences.zh: 楊廷和，字介夫，新都人。

translations.literal: Yang Tinghe, styled Jiefu, was a native of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tinghe, whose style was Jiefu, came from Xindu.

sentences.zh: 父春，湖廣提學僉事。

translations.literal: His father Chun was an assistant education intendant in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yang Chun had served as an assistant education intendant in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 廷和年十二舉於鄉。

translations.literal: Tinghe passed the provincial examination at the age of twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe passed the provincial civil service examination when he was only twelve.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年，年十九，先其父成進士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chenghua, at nineteen, he became a jinshi before his father.
translations.idiomatic: In 1478, at nineteen, he passed the metropolitan examination and became a jinshi before his father did.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，告歸娶，還朝授檢討。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin academician-expositor, returned home to marry, and on coming back to court was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Hanlin academician-expositor, went home to marry, and on returning to court was appointed a reviser in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 廷和為人美風姿，性沈靜詳審，為文簡暢有法。

translations.literal: Tinghe was handsome in bearing, calm and thorough in disposition, and wrote in a concise, fluent, and well-regulated style.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe was a man of fine presence, calm and meticulous by nature, and his writing was concise, fluent, and disciplined.

sentences.zh: 好考究掌故、民瘼、邊事及一切法家言，郁然負公輔望。

translations.literal: He delighted in investigating precedents, the people's hardships, frontier affairs, and all legalist writings, and bore the air of one destined for high ministerial office.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to study historical precedents, the people's grievances, frontier affairs, and the whole body of legalist thought, and he already carried himself like a future chief minister.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年進修撰。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongzhi he was promoted to compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1489 he was promoted to compiler in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 《憲宗實錄》成，以預纂修進侍讀。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong were completed, he was advanced to reader-in-waiting for having taken part in the compilation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of the Chenghua reign were finished, he was promoted to reader-in-waiting for his work on the project.

sentences.zh: 改左春坊左中允，侍皇太子講讀。

translations.literal: He was transferred to left assistant in the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent and attended the crown prince in his lectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was made left assistant in the Eastern Palace and attended the crown prince's lectures.

sentences.zh: 修《會典》成，超拜左春坊大學士，充日講官。

translations.literal: When the compilation of the Collected Statutes was completed, he was specially promoted to grand secretary of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent and appointed a daily lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Collected Statutes were completed, he was promoted out of turn to grand secretary of the Eastern Palace and made a daily lecturer at court.

sentences.zh: 正德二年由詹事入東閣，專典誥敕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde he entered the Eastern Pavilion from the post of tutor of the heir apparent and was put in charge of edicts and patents of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: In 1507 he entered the Eastern Pavilion from the post of tutor of the heir apparent and was put in sole charge of drafting edicts and patents of nobility.

sentences.zh: 以講筵指斥佞幸，忤劉瑾，傳旨改南京吏部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Because at the lecture he denounced the sycophants and offended Liu Jin, an imperial order transferred him to left vice minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At a lecture he denounced the emperor's favorites and offended Liu Jin, who had him transferred by imperial order to left vice minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 五月遷南京戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was transferred to minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Five months later he was made minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 又三月召還，進兼文淵閣大學士，參預機務。

translations.literal: Three months later he was recalled, advanced to concurrent grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, and allowed to participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Three months after that he was recalled, made concurrent grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, and admitted to deliberations on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年加少保兼太子太保。

translations.literal: The next year he was given the additional titles of Junior Guardian and concurrent Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was given the additional titles of Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 瑾摘《會典》小誤，奪廷和與大學士李東陽等俸二級。

translations.literal: Jin seized on minor errors in the Collected Statutes and stripped Tinghe and the grand secretary Li Dongyang and others of two ranks of salary.
translations.idiomatic: Jin seized on minor errors in the Collected Statutes and cut Tinghe's salary, along with that of Grand Secretary Li Dongyang and others, by two grades.

sentences.zh: 尋以成《孝宗實錄》功還之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, for completing the Veritable Records of Emperor Xiaozong, their salaries were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward their salaries were restored for their work on the Veritable Records of the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 明年加光祿大夫、柱國，遷改吏部尚書、武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: The next year he was given the titles of Grand Master for Glorious Blessing and Pillar of the State, and was transferred to minister of the Ministry of Personnel and grand secretary of the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he received the titles of Grand Master for Glorious Blessing and Pillar of the State and was made minister of the Ministry of Personnel and grand secretary of the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 時瑾橫益甚，而焦芳、張糸采為中外媾。

translations.literal: At that time Jin grew ever more overbearing, while Jiao Fang and Zhang Cai served as go-betweens inside and outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: By then Jin was growing ever more tyrannical, while Jiao Fang and Zhang Cai acted as liaisons between the inner and outer courts.

sentences.zh: 廷和與東陽委曲其間，小有劑救而已。

translations.literal: Tinghe and Dongyang maneuvered tactfully among them and could offer only slight remedies.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe and Li Dongyang had to maneuver tactfully among them and could manage only small acts of relief.

sentences.zh: 安化王寘鐇反，以誅瑾為名。

translations.literal: The Prince of Anhua, Zhu Zhifan, rebelled, taking the execution of Jin as his rallying cry.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Anhua, Zhu Zhifan, rebelled under the banner of executing Liu Jin.

sentences.zh: 廷和等草赦詔，請擢邊將仇鉞，以離賊黨。

translations.literal: Tinghe and the others drafted an amnesty edict and asked that the frontier general Qiu Yue be promoted to divide the rebel faction.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe and his colleagues drafted an amnesty edict and urged that the frontier general Qiu Yue be promoted so as to split the rebel ranks.

sentences.zh: 鉞果執寘鐇。

translations.literal: Qiu indeed captured Zhifan.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu did in fact capture Zhifan.

sentences.zh: 會張永發瑾罪，瑾伏誅，廷和等乃復論功，進少傅兼太子太傅、謹身殿大學士，予一子中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yong exposed Jin's crimes and Jin was executed, Tinghe and the others were again rewarded for merit, advanced to Junior Mentor and concurrent Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and grand secretary of the Jinshen Hall, and granted one son the post of secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yong exposed Jin's crimes and Jin was put to death, Tinghe and his colleagues were again rewarded: he was made Junior Mentor and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and grand secretary of the Jinshen Hall, and one of his sons was granted the post of secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 流賊劉六、劉七、齊彥名反，楊一清薦馬中錫討之。

translations.literal: The bandit leaders Liu Liu, Liu Qi, and Qi Yanming rebelled, and Yang Yiqing recommended Ma Zhongxi to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit leaders Liu Liu, Liu Qi, and Qi Yanming rose in revolt, and Yang Yiqing recommended Ma Zhongxi to put them down.

sentences.zh: 廷和言：「中錫，文士也，不任此。」

translations.literal: Tinghe said, "Zhongxi is a literary man and is not fit for this.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe said, "Zhongxi is a scholar-official and is not equal to this task.

sentences.zh: 時業已行，果不能平賊。

translations.literal: The appointment had already been made, and indeed he could not pacify the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment had already gone out, and as Tinghe had warned, he failed to pacify the bandits.

sentences.zh: 廷和請逮中錫下獄，以陸完代之，而斬故受賕縱賊者參將桑玉。

translations.literal: Tinghe asked that Zhongxi be arrested and imprisoned, that Lu Wan replace him, and that the former vice commander Sang Yu, who had taken bribes and let the bandits escape, be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe asked that Zhongxi be arrested and imprisoned, that Lu Wan replace him, and that the former vice commander Sang Yu, who had taken bribes and let the bandits escape, be executed.

sentences.zh: 已，又用學士陳霽言，調諸邊兵討河南賊趙鐩等，而薦彭澤為總制。

translations.literal: Later, following the advice of the academician Chen Ji, he transferred troops from the frontiers to campaign against the Henan bandits Zhao Secheng and others, and recommended Peng Ze as supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: Later, following Academician Chen Ji's advice, he transferred frontier troops to campaign against the Henan bandits led by Zhao Secheng and recommended Peng Ze as supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 賊平論功，錄廷和一子錦衣衛千戶。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified and merit was assessed, one of Tinghe's sons was enrolled as a chiliarch in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits were pacified and rewards were distributed, one of Tinghe's sons was enrolled as a chiliarch in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 辭，特加少師、太子太師、華蓋殿大學士。

translations.literal: He declined, and was specially given the titles of Junior Preceptor, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and grand secretary of the Huagai Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the hereditary post and was instead given the titles of Junior Preceptor, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and grand secretary of the Huagai Hall.

sentences.zh: 東陽致政，廷和遂為首輔。

translations.literal: Dongyang retired from office, and Tinghe became the chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Dongyang retired, Tinghe became chief grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 張永既去瑾而驕，捕得男子臂龍文者以為功，援故太監劉永誠例，覬封侯。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong, having removed Jin, grew arrogant; he captured a man with a dragon pattern on his arm and claimed it as merit, citing the precedent of the former eunuch Liu Yongcheng, and sought enfeoffment as a marquis.
translations.idiomatic: After helping bring down Jin, Zhang Yong grew arrogant; he seized a man with a dragon tattoo on his arm and claimed it as a great exploit, citing the precedent of the former eunuch Liu Yongcheng, and sought to be enfeoffed as a marquis.

sentences.zh: 廷和言「永誠從子聚自以戰功封伯耳，且非永誠身受之也」，乃止。

translations.literal: Tinghe said, "Yongcheng's nephew Ju was enfeoffed as a count only for military merit, and even that was not a title Yongcheng himself received," and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe replied that "Yongcheng's nephew Ju was enfeoffed as a count only for military merit, and even that was not a title Yongcheng himself received," and the request was dropped.

sentences.zh: 彭澤將西討鄢本恕，問計廷和。

translations.literal: Peng Ze was about to campaign west against Yan Benshu and asked Tinghe for counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng Ze was about to march west against Yan Benshu, he asked Tinghe for advice.

sentences.zh: 廷和曰：「以君才，賊不足平，所戒者班師早耳。」

translations.literal: Tinghe said, "With your ability the bandits are not hard to pacify; what you must guard against is withdrawing the army too soon.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe said, "With your ability the rebels are not hard to defeat; what you must guard against is withdrawing too soon.

sentences.zh: 澤後破誅本恕等即班師，而余黨復猬起不可制。

translations.literal: Later Ze defeated and executed Benshu and the others and then withdrew, whereupon the remaining partisans rose again like hedgehogs and could not be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze later defeated and killed Benshu and his followers and then withdrew, whereupon the remaining rebels flared up again and could no longer be controlled.

sentences.zh: 澤既發復留，乃嘆曰：「楊公先見，吾不及也。」

translations.literal: Ze had already set out but turned back to stay, and sighed, "Master Yang foresaw this; I fell short of him."
translations.idiomatic: Having already set out, Peng Ze turned back to remain on campaign and sighed, "Master Yang saw this coming; I was not his equal."

sentences.zh: 乾清宮災，廷和請帝避殿，下詔罪己，求直言。

translations.literal: When the Qianqing Palace burned, Tinghe asked the emperor to move to another hall, issue an edict blaming himself, and seek forthright counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When fire destroyed the Qianqing Palace, Tinghe urged the emperor to move to another hall, issue a self-reproach edict, and invite frank criticism.

sentences.zh: 因與其僚上疏，勸帝早朝晏罷，躬九廟祭祀，崇兩宮孝養，勤日講。

translations.literal: He and his colleagues then submitted a memorial urging the emperor to hold early audiences and end court late, personally perform sacrifices at the nine ancestral temples, honor both palaces in filial devotion, and attend diligently to the daily lectures.
translations.idiomatic: He and his colleagues then submitted a memorial urging the emperor to hold early audiences and end court late, perform sacrifices at the nine ancestral temples in person, honor both palaces in filial devotion, and attend diligently to the daily lectures.

sentences.zh: 復面奏開言路、達下情、還邊兵、革宮市、罷皇店、出西僧、省工作、減織造，凡十余條，皆切至。

translations.literal: He also memorialized in person to open channels of remonstrance, convey the people's condition, return frontier troops, abolish palace markets, close imperial shops, expel Western monks, reduce construction, and cut textile manufacture—more than ten items in all, each pointed and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke in person to open channels of remonstrance, convey the people's condition, return frontier troops, abolish palace markets, close imperial shops, expel Western monks, reduce construction, and cut textile manufacture—more than ten proposals in all, each pointed and urgent.

sentences.zh: 帝不省。

translations.literal: The emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 尋以父卒乞奔喪，不許。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on his father's death, he asked leave to rush home for mourning and was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when his father died, he asked leave to rush home for mourning and was refused.

sentences.zh: 三請乃許。

translations.literal: Only after three requests was permission granted.
translations.idiomatic: Only after three requests was he allowed to go.

sentences.zh: 遣中官護行。

translations.literal: A palace eunuch was sent to escort him on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent a palace eunuch to escort him on the journey.

sentences.zh: 旋復起之，三疏辭，始許。

translations.literal: He was soon recalled to office; after three memorials declining, he was at last allowed to remain in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to office, but after three memorials declining the summons he was at last allowed to remain in mourning.

sentences.zh: 閣臣之得終父母喪者，自廷和始也。

translations.literal: Tinghe was the first grand secretary allowed to complete mourning for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He was the first grand secretary in living memory allowed to complete the full mourning period for his parents.

sentences.zh: 服甫闋，即召至。

translations.literal: As soon as his mourning period had barely ended, he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had his mourning ended when he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 帝方獵宣府，使使賜廷和羊酒、銀幣。

translations.literal: The emperor was then hunting at Xuanfu and sent envoys to bestow on Tinghe mutton, wine, silver, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was hunting at Xuanfu and sent envoys to reward Tinghe with mutton, wine, silver, and silks.

sentences.zh: 廷和疏謝，因請回鑾，不報。

translations.literal: Tinghe memorialized his thanks and asked that the imperial procession return; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe thanked him in a memorial and asked that the imperial procession return; he received no answer.

sentences.zh: 復與大學士蔣冕馳至居庸，欲身出塞請。

translations.literal: He again rushed with Grand Secretary Jiang Mian to Juyong Pass, intending to go beyond the frontier in person to plead.
translations.idiomatic: He then rushed with Grand Secretary Jiang Mian to Juyong Pass, intending to go beyond the frontier in person to plead with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝令谷大用扼關門，乃歸。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Gu Dayong to hold the pass gate, and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Gu Dayong to block the pass, and they had to turn back.

sentences.zh: 帝命回鑾日群臣各制旗帳迎，廷和曰：「此裏俗以施之親舊耳。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that on the day of his return every official should prepare banners and canopies to welcome him. Tinghe said, "This is a village custom used for relatives and friends.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that on the day of his return every official should prepare banners and canopies to welcome him. Tinghe said, "That is a village custom for relatives and friends.

sentences.zh: 天子至尊，不敢瀆獻。」

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven is supreme; I dare not offer such a thing irreverently.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven is supreme; I dare not offer such a thing irreverently.

sentences.zh: 帝再使使諭意，執不從，乃已。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent envoys to explain his wish, but Tinghe stood firm and would not comply, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys again to explain his wish, but Tinghe stood firm and would not comply, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 當廷和柄政，帝恒不視朝，恣遊大同、宣府、延綏間，多失政。

translations.literal: While Tinghe held power, the emperor constantly neglected court audiences and roamed at will among Datong, Xuanfu, and Yansui, committing many abuses of government.
translations.idiomatic: While Tinghe held power, the emperor constantly neglected court audiences and roamed at will through Datong, Xuanfu, and Yansui, and government suffered accordingly.

sentences.zh: 廷和未嘗不諫，俱不聽。

translations.literal: Tinghe never failed to remonstrate, but none of it was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe remonstrated again and again, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 廷和亦不能執奏。

translations.literal: Nor could Tinghe press his views by insisting on memorializing.
translations.idiomatic: Nor could Tinghe force the issue by insisting on memorializing.

sentences.zh: 以是邑邑不自得，數移疾乞骸骨，帝亦不聽。

translations.literal: For this reason he was depressed and ill at ease, and several times asked leave on grounds of illness to retire; the emperor would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: He grew depressed and uneasy, and several times asked to retire on grounds of illness, but the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 中官谷大用、魏彬、張雄，義子錢寧、江彬輩，恣橫甚。

translations.literal: The eunuchs Gu Dayong, Wei Bin, and Zhang Xiong, and the adopted sons Qian Ning, Jiang Bin, and their like, were extremely overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs Gu Dayong, Wei Bin, and Zhang Xiong, together with the emperor's favorites Qian Ning, Jiang Bin, and their like, ran wild.

sentences.zh: 廷和雖不為下，然亦不能有所裁禁，以是得稍自安。

translations.literal: Although Tinghe did not submit to them, he likewise could not restrain them, and for that reason was able to gain a little peace.
translations.idiomatic: Although Tinghe did not submit to them, he could not restrain them either, and for that reason he was left in relative peace.

sentences.zh: 御史蕭淮發寧王宸濠反謀，錢寧輩猶庇之，詆淮離間。

translations.literal: The censor Xiao Huai exposed the Prince of Ning Zhu Chenhao's plot to rebel, but Qian Ning and his faction still shielded him and slandered Huai for sowing discord.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xiao Huai exposed the Prince of Ning Zhu Chenhao's plot to rebel, but Qian Ning and his faction still shielded the prince and accused Huai of sowing discord.

sentences.zh: 廷和請如宣宗諭趙王故事，遣貴戚大臣賫敕往諭，收其護衛屯田。

translations.literal: Tinghe asked that, following the precedent of Emperor Xuanzong's admonition to the Prince of Zhao, an imperial kinsman or high minister be sent bearing an edict to instruct him and seize his guard troops and military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe proposed following the precedent of Emperor Xuanzong's admonition to the Prince of Zhao: send a royal kinsman or senior minister with an edict to warn the prince and seize his guard troops and military colonies.

sentences.zh: 於是命中官賴義、駙馬都尉崔元等往，未至而宸濠反。

translations.literal: The court then appointed the eunuch Lai Yi, the emperor's son-in-law Cui Yuan, and others to go, but before they arrived Chenhao rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The court then sent the eunuch Lai Yi, the emperor's son-in-law Cui Yuan, and others, but before they arrived Chenhao had already rebelled.

sentences.zh: 帝欲帥師親征，廷和等力阻之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to lead the army in person, and Tinghe and the others strongly opposed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to lead the army in person, and Tinghe and his colleagues strongly opposed it.

sentences.zh: 帝乃自稱總督軍務、威武大將軍、總兵官、後軍都督府、太師、鎮國公朱壽，統各京邊將士南討。

translations.literal: The emperor then styled himself Supervisor of Military Affairs, Awesome-and-Mighty Grand General, Commander-in-Chief, Rear Army Commander-in-Chief, Grand Preceptor, and Defender of the State Duke Zhu Shou, and led the generals and troops of the capital and frontiers south to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then took the titles Supervisor of Military Affairs, Awesome-and-Mighty Grand General, Commander-in-Chief, Rear Army Commander-in-Chief, Grand Preceptor, and Defender of the State Duke Zhu Shou, and led the capital and frontier armies south.

sentences.zh: 而安邊伯許泰為威武副將軍、左都督劉暉為平賊將軍前驅，鎮守、撫、按悉聽節制。

translations.literal: The Defender of the Border Earl Xu Tai was made Awesome-and-Mighty Vice General, and the left chief commander Liu Hui was made Pacification General in the vanguard; all regional commanders, grand coordinators, and surveillance commissioners were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Tai, Earl Defender of the Border, was made Awesome-and-Mighty Vice General, and Liu Hui, left chief commander, was made Pacification General in the vanguard; all regional commanders, grand coordinators, and surveillance commissioners were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 命廷和與大學士毛紀居守。

translations.literal: Tinghe and Grand Secretary Mao Ji were ordered to remain and guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe and Grand Secretary Mao Ji were ordered to remain in the capital as regents.

sentences.zh: 以乾清、坤寧二宮工成，推恩錄一子錦衣衛副千戶，辭。

translations.literal: Because the Qianqing and Kunning palaces had been completed, an enfeoffment granted one of his sons the post of vice chiliarch in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard; he declined.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianqing and Kunning palaces were completed, he was granted an enfeoffment enrolling one of his sons as a vice chiliarch in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard; he declined.

sentences.zh: 時廷和當草大將軍征南敕諭，謝弗肯，帝心恚。

translations.literal: At that time Tinghe was to draft the Grand General's southern campaign edict of instruction, but he declined and refused; the emperor was resentful at heart.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Tinghe was expected to draft the Grand General's southern campaign edict, but he refused; the emperor took it ill.

sentences.zh: 會推南京吏部尚書劉春理東閣誥敕，以廷和私其鄉人，切責之。

translations.literal: When the Nanjing minister of personnel Liu Chun was recommended to manage Eastern Pavilion edicts and patents, the emperor sharply rebuked Tinghe for favoring a fellow townsman.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing Minister of Personnel Liu Chun was recommended to manage Eastern Pavilion edicts and patents, the emperor sharply rebuked Tinghe for favoring a fellow townsman.

sentences.zh: 廷和謝罪，乞罷，不許。

translations.literal: Tinghe apologized and asked to resign; permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe apologized and asked to resign, but the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 少師梁儲等請與俱罷，復不許。

translations.literal: Junior Preceptor Liang Chu and others asked to resign with him; again permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Preceptor Liang Chu and others asked to resign with him; again the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 廷和方引疾不入，帝遂傳旨行之。

translations.literal: Tinghe was then pleading illness and would not enter court, so the emperor transmitted an order and carried the appointment through.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe was then pleading illness and would not come to court, so the emperor issued an order and carried the appointment through without him.

sentences.zh: 時十四年八月也。

translations.literal: This was in the eighth month of the fourteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the eighth month of the fourteenth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 帝既南，兩更歲朔。

translations.literal: After the emperor went south, two New Year observances passed.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor marched south, two New Year observances passed.

sentences.zh: 廷和頗以鎮靜持重，為中外所推服。

translations.literal: Tinghe was much admired inside and outside the court for his calm steadiness.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe won wide respect inside and outside the court for his calm steadiness.

sentences.zh: 凡請回鑾者數十疏，皆不復省。

translations.literal: Several tens of memorials asking that the imperial procession return were all left unread.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of memorials asking that the imperial procession return went unread.

sentences.zh: 帝歸，駐蹕通州。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned, he halted at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, he halted at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 廷和等舉故事，請帝還大內御殿受俘，然後正宸濠等誅，而帝已不豫。

translations.literal: Tinghe and the others cited precedent and asked that the emperor return to the inner palace to receive the captives in audience and then carry out the proper punishment of Chenhao and the others, but the emperor was already unwell.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe and his colleagues cited precedent and asked that the emperor return to the inner palace to receive the captives in audience before punishing Chenhao and the others, but the emperor was already unwell.

sentences.zh: 趨召廷和等至通州受事，即行在執宸濠等僇之，駕乃旋。

translations.literal: He urgently summoned Tinghe and the others to Tongzhou to take charge; they immediately executed Chenhao and the others at the traveling palace, and only then did the imperial carriage turn back.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently summoned Tinghe and his colleagues to Tongzhou to take charge; they immediately executed Chenhao and his followers at the traveling palace, and only then did the imperial carriage turn back.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，帝郊祀，嘔血輿疾歸，逾月益篤。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year the emperor performed suburban sacrifice, vomited blood, and was carried back ill; after more than a month his condition grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year the emperor performed the suburban sacrifice, vomited blood, and was carried back to the palace ill; after more than a month his condition worsened.

sentences.zh: 時帝無嗣。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had no heir.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no heir.

sentences.zh: 司禮中官魏彬等至閣言：「國醫力竭矣，請捐萬金購之草澤。」

translations.literal: The Directorate eunuchs Wei Bin and others came to the Grand Secretariat and said, "The imperial physicians have exhausted their strength; please donate ten thousand taels of silver to seek a remedy among the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate eunuchs led by Wei Bin came to the Grand Secretariat and said, "The imperial physicians have done all they can; please donate ten thousand taels of silver to seek a remedy among the common people.

sentences.zh: 廷和心知所謂，不應，而微以倫序之說風之，彬等唯唯。

translations.literal: Tinghe knew what they meant, made no reply, but subtly admonished them with the doctrine of succession; Bin and the others murmured assent.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe understood what they meant, made no direct reply, but subtly admonished them with the doctrine of succession; Wei Bin and the others murmured assent.

sentences.zh: 三月十四日丙寅，谷大用、張永至閣，言帝崩於豹房。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day of the third month, the day bingyin, Gu Dayong and Zhang Yong came to the Grand Secretariat and announced that the emperor had died in the Leopard Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth day of the third month, Gu Dayong and Zhang Yong came to the Grand Secretariat and announced that the emperor had died in the Leopard Quarters.

sentences.zh: 以皇太后命，移殯大內，且議所當立。

translations.literal: By the empress dowager's order the coffin was moved to the inner palace, and deliberation began on who should be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: By the empress dowager's order the coffin was moved to the inner palace, and deliberation began on who should succeed.

sentences.zh: 廷和舉《皇明祖訓》示之曰：「兄終弟及，誰能瀆焉！

translations.literal: Tinghe produced the Ancestral Instructions of the August Ming and showed them, saying, "When an elder brother ends his reign, a younger brother succeeds—who can violate this!
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe produced the Ancestral Instructions of the August Ming and said, "When an elder brother ends his reign, a younger brother succeeds—who can violate that rule?

sentences.zh: 興獻王長子，憲宗之孫，孝宗之從子，大行皇帝之從弟，序當立。」

translations.literal: The eldest son of the Prince of Xingxian is a grandson of Emperor Xianzong, a grandnephew of Emperor Xiaozong, and a younger cousin of the late emperor; by order he should be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son of the Prince of Xingxian is a grandson of Emperor Xianzong, a grandnephew of Emperor Xiaozong, and a younger cousin of the late emperor; by right he should succeed.

sentences.zh: 梁儲、蔣冕、毛紀鹹贊之。

translations.literal: Liang Chu, Jiang Mian, and Mao Ji all approved.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chu, Jiang Mian, and Mao Ji all agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃令中官入啟皇太后，廷和等候左順門下。

translations.literal: They then had a eunuch enter to inform the empress dowager, while Tinghe and the others waited below the Left Gate of Compliance.
translations.idiomatic: They then sent a eunuch in to inform the empress dowager, while Tinghe and the others waited below the Left Gate of Compliance.

sentences.zh: 頃之，中官奉遺詔及太后懿旨，宣諭群臣，一如廷和請，事乃定。

translations.literal: Before long a eunuch brought the testamentary edict and the empress dowager's decree and proclaimed them to the officials; all was as Tinghe had proposed, and the matter was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a eunuch brought the testamentary edict and the empress dowager's decree and proclaimed them to the officials; everything was as Tinghe had proposed, and the succession was settled.

sentences.zh: 廷和遂以遺詔令太監張永、武定侯郭勛、安邊伯許泰、尚書王憲選各營兵，分布皇城四門、京城九門及南北要害，廣衛御史以其屬捍掫。

translations.literal: Tinghe then, by the testamentary edict, ordered the eunuch Zhang Yong, the Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun, the Earl Defender of the Border Xu Tai, and the minister Wang Xian to select troops from each camp and deploy them at the four gates of the Imperial City, the nine gates of the capital, and the key points north and south; surveillance censors of the Broad Surveillance Office posted their subordinates to guard and patrol.
translations.idiomatic: By the testamentary edict Tinghe ordered the eunuch Zhang Yong, the Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun, the Earl Defender of the Border Xu Tai, and Minister Wang Xian to select troops from each camp and deploy them at the four gates of the Imperial City, the nine gates of the capital, and other key points; surveillance censors posted their subordinates to guard and patrol.

sentences.zh: 傳遺命罷威武營團練諸軍，各邊兵入衛者俱重賚散歸鎮，革皇店及軍門辦事官校悉還衛，哈密、土魯番、佛郎機諸貢使皆給賞遣還國，豹房番僧及少林僧、教坊樂人、南京快馬船、諸非常例者，一切罷遣。

translations.literal: By the dying command he abolished the Awesome-and-Mighty Battalion and all drilled troops, richly rewarded frontier troops who had entered to guard the capital and sent them back to their posts, abolished imperial shops and returned all military-gate clerks and runners to their guards, gave rewards and sent home the tribute envoys of Hami, Turfan, and Portugal, and dismissed altogether the Western monks of the Leopard Quarters and Shaolin, the music-office performers, the Nanjing fast horse-boats, and all other irregular practices.
translations.idiomatic: By the dying command he abolished the Awesome-and-Mighty Battalion and all drilled troops, richly rewarded frontier troops who had come to guard the capital and sent them back to their posts, abolished imperial shops and returned military-gate clerks and runners to their guards, rewarded and sent home the tribute envoys from Hami, Turfan, and Portugal, and dismissed altogether the Western monks of the Leopard Quarters and Shaolin, the music-office performers, the Nanjing fast horse-boats, and all other irregular practices.

sentences.zh: 又以遺詔釋南京逮擊囚，放遣四方進獻女子，停京師不急工務，收宣府行宮金寶歸諸內庫。

translations.literal: By the testamentary edict he also released prisoners held in Nanjing, sent away women presented from all quarters, halted non-urgent construction in the capital, and returned the gold and jewels of the Xuanfu traveling palace to the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The testamentary edict also released prisoners held in Nanjing, sent away women presented from all quarters, halted non-urgent construction in the capital, and returned the gold and jewels of the Xuanfu traveling palace to the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 中外大悅。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court there was great rejoicing.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country alike rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 時平虜伯江彬擁重兵在肘腋間，知天下惡之，心不自安。

translations.literal: At the time Jiang Bin, Pacification Baron, held a heavy force close at hand; knowing that the empire hated him, he was ill at ease in heart.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jiang Bin, Pacification Baron, held a large army at the emperor's very side; knowing how widely he was hated, he grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 其黨都督僉事李琮尤狠黠，勸彬乘間以其家眾反，不勝則北走塞外。

translations.literal: Among his partisans, Vice Commander Li Cong was especially fierce and cunning; he urged Bin to seize an opportunity and rebel with his household following, and if unsuccessful to flee north beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: His follower, Vice Commander Li Cong, was especially ruthless and shrewd; he urged Jiang Bin to seize an opening and rise in rebellion with his household troops, and if defeated to flee north into the borderlands.

sentences.zh: 彬猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Bin hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bin hesitated and could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 於是廷和謀以皇太后旨捕誅彬，遂與同官蔣冕、毛紀及司禮中官溫祥四人謀。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tinghe plotted to capture and execute Bin by the empress dowager's order, and together with his colleagues Jiang Mian and Mao Ji and the Directorate eunuch Wen Xiang the four of them took counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe then plotted to arrest and execute Jiang Bin by order of the empress dowager, taking counsel with his colleagues Jiang Mian and Mao Ji and the Directorate eunuch Wen Xiang.

sentences.zh: 張永伺知其意，亦密為備。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong detected their intent and also secretly made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong detected their intent and also made secret preparations.

sentences.zh: 司禮魏彬者，故與彬有連。

translations.literal: The Directorate eunuch Wei Bin had formerly been connected with Jiang Bin.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate eunuch Wei Bin had formerly been allied with Jiang Bin.

sentences.zh: 廷和以其弱可脅也，因題大行銘旌，與彬、祥及他中官張銳、陳嚴等為詳言江彬反狀，以危語怵之。

translations.literal: Tinghe thought him weak and could be intimidated; he therefore inscribed the mourning banner for the late emperor and, with Wei Bin, Wen Xiang, and the other eunuchs Zhang Rui and Chen Yan, gave a detailed account of Jiang Bin's rebellious conduct, frightening them with alarming words.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe judged Wei Bin weak and susceptible to pressure; he therefore inscribed the late emperor's mourning banner and, with Wei Bin, Wen Xiang, and the other eunuchs Zhang Rui and Chen Yan, laid out Jiang Bin's treason in detail, terrifying them with dire warnings.

sentences.zh: 彬心動，惟銳力言江彬無罪，廷和面折之。

translations.literal: Wei Bin's heart was moved, but Rui alone strongly argued that Jiang Bin was innocent; Tinghe rebutted him to his face.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bin wavered, but Zhang Rui alone insisted that Jiang Bin was innocent; Tinghe openly confronted him.

sentences.zh: 冕曰：「今日必了此，乃臨。」

translations.literal: Mian said, "This must be settled today, and only then may we attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Mian said, "This must be settled today before we go to court.

sentences.zh: 嚴亦從旁贊決，因俾祥、彬等入白皇太后。

translations.literal: Yan also spoke from the side urging a decision, and had Wen Xiang, Wei Bin, and the others enter to report to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yan also seconded the decision from the side, and sent Wen Xiang, Wei Bin, and the others in to inform the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 良久未報，廷和、冕益自危。

translations.literal: A long time passed with no reply; Tinghe and Mian grew ever more fearful for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: A long time passed with no answer, and Tinghe and Jiang Mian grew increasingly alarmed.

sentences.zh: 頃之，嚴至曰：「彬已擒矣。」

translations.literal: Before long Yan arrived and said, "Bin has already been captured.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chen Yan came and said, "Jiang Bin has already been seized.

sentences.zh: 彬既誅，中外相慶。

translations.literal: Once Bin had been executed, court and country alike rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jiang Bin had been put to death, the court and the empire rejoiced together.

sentences.zh: 廷和總朝政幾四十日，興世子始入京師即帝位。

translations.literal: Tinghe directed court affairs for nearly forty days before the heir of the Prince of Xing entered the capital and took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe directed the government for nearly forty days before the heir of the Prince of Xing entered the capital and ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 廷和草上登極詔書，文書房官忽至閣中，言欲去詔中不便者數事。

translations.literal: Tinghe drafted the accession edict; an officer of the Document Drafting Office suddenly came to the Grand Secretariat and said he wished to remove several inconvenient items from the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe drafted the accession edict; an officer from the Document Drafting Office suddenly appeared in the Grand Secretariat and said he wanted to strike several inconvenient passages from the draft.

sentences.zh: 廷和曰：「往者事齟齬，動稱上意。

translations.literal: Tinghe said, "Formerly, whenever matters went awry, it was always called the emperor's will.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe said, "In the past, whenever matters went awry, it was always called the emperor's will.

sentences.zh: 今亦新天子意耶？

translations.literal: Is this now the new Son of Heaven's will as well?
translations.idiomatic: Is this the new emperor's will as well?

sentences.zh: 吾儕賀登極後，當面奏上，問誰欲削詔草者！」

translations.literal: After we have congratulated the accession, we shall memorialize the throne in person and ask who wishes to cut items from the draft edict!
translations.idiomatic: After we have offered our congratulations on the accession, we shall memorialize the throne in person and ask who wants to cut passages from the draft edict!

sentences.zh: 冕、紀亦相繼發危言，其人語塞。

translations.literal: Mian and Ji also successively spoke stern words, and the man was left speechless.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Mian and Mao Ji also spoke sternly in turn, and the man was left without a reply.

sentences.zh: 已而詔下，正德中蠹政厘抉且盡。

translations.literal: Before long the edict was issued, and the corrupt policies of the Zhengde reign were sorted out and nearly all eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the edict was promulgated, and the corrupt practices of the Zhengde reign were rooted out almost entirely.

sentences.zh: 所裁汰錦衣諸衛、內監局旗校工役為數十四萬八千七百，減漕糧百五十三萬二千余石。

translations.literal: Those cut included bannermen, runners, and laborers of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and other guards and of the inner palace offices, numbering 148,700 in all, and grain transport tribute was reduced by more than 1,532,000 shi.
translations.idiomatic: The cuts eliminated 148,700 bannermen, runners, and laborers from the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and other guards and from the inner palace offices, and reduced grain transport tribute by more than 1,532,000 shi.

sentences.zh: 其中貴、義子、傳升、乞升一切恩幸得官者大半皆斥去。

translations.literal: Inner favorites, adopted sons, and all who had received office through transferred promotion, petitioned promotion, and other favor—all such beneficiaries—were for the most part dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Inner favorites, adopted sons, and the many who had gained office through transferred promotions, petitioned promotions, and other imperial favor were for the most part dismissed.

sentences.zh: 中外稱新天子「聖人」，且頌廷和功。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court called the new Son of Heaven a "Sage," and also praised Tinghe's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country alike hailed the new emperor as a "Sage," and praised Tinghe's achievement as well.

sentences.zh: 而諸失職之徒銜廷和次骨，廷和入朝有挾白刃伺輿旁者。

translations.literal: But those who had lost their posts hated Tinghe to the bone; when Tinghe entered court, someone with a bare blade waited beside his sedan chair.
translations.idiomatic: But those who had lost their positions hated Tinghe bitterly; when he came to court, a man with a bare blade waited beside his sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔以營卒百人衛出入。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict ordered a hundred camp soldiers to guard his comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, an edict ordered a hundred camp soldiers to guard him whenever he went out or returned.

sentences.zh: 帝御經筵，廷和知經筵事。

translations.literal: The emperor attended the Classics Lectures, and Tinghe directed Classics Lectures affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor attended the Classics Lectures, and Tinghe was placed in charge of them.

sentences.zh: 修《武宗實錄》，充總裁。

translations.literal: He compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Wuzong and served as chief compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw compilation of the Veritable Records of Emperor Wuzong as chief compiler.

sentences.zh: 廷和先已加特進，一品滿九載，兼支大學士俸，賜敕旌諭。

translations.literal: Tinghe had already been granted Supernumerary Promotion; after nine years at the first rank he concurrently drew a grand secretary's salary and was granted an edict of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe had already been granted Supernumerary Promotion; after nine years at the first rank he drew a grand secretary's salary as well and received an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 至是加左柱國。

translations.literal: At this time he was further made Left Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: At this point he was further promoted to Left Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 帝召對者三，慰勞備至。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him for audience three times and comforted him with the utmost kindness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him for private audience three times and comforted him with exceptional warmth.

sentences.zh: 廷和益欲有所發攄，引用正人，布列在位。

translations.literal: Tinghe wished all the more to give full expression to his aims, recommend upright men, and deploy them in office.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe wished all the more to act boldly, bring in upright men, and place them throughout the government.

sentences.zh: 給事、御史交章論王瓊罪狀，下詔獄。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries and censors submitted memorial after memorial setting forth Wang Qiong's crimes, and he was sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries and censors submitted memorial after memorial detailing Wang Qiong's crimes, and he was sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 瓊迫，疏訐廷和以自解。

translations.literal: Qiong, pressed hard, memorialized slandering Tinghe to exculpate himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Wang Qiong memorialized the throne slandering Tinghe in an effort to save himself.

sentences.zh: 法司當瓊奸黨律論死，瓊力自辨，得減戍邊。

translations.literal: The legal offices judged Qiong under the law on treacherous factions as deserving death; Qiong vigorously defended himself and the sentence was reduced to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: The legal offices judged Wang Qiong under the law on treacherous factions as deserving death; he defended himself vigorously and the sentence was reduced to exile on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 或疑法司承廷和指者。

translations.literal: Some suspected that the legal offices were acting on Tinghe's instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Some suspected that the legal offices were acting at Tinghe's direction.

sentences.zh: 會石缶自禮部尚書掌詹事府，改吏部，廷和復奏改之掌詹事司誥敕。

translations.literal: When Shi Fu moved from minister of rites and director of the Directorate of the Heir Apparent to the Ministry of Personnel, Tinghe again memorialized that he be changed to direct patents and edicts in the Directorate of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Jiubao moved from the Ministry of Rites and the Directorate of the Heir Apparent to the Ministry of Personnel, Tinghe again memorialized that he be reassigned to manage patents and edicts in the Directorate of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 人或謂廷和太專。

translations.literal: Some said Tinghe was too autocratic.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Tinghe had grown too domineering.

sentences.zh: 然廷和以帝雖沖年，性英敏，自信可輔太平，事事有所持諍。

translations.literal: Yet Tinghe considered that although the emperor was young, his nature was bright and keen; confident that he could assist in bringing about great peace, he remonstrated firmly in every matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Tinghe believed that although the emperor was young, he was bright and quick-witted; confident that he could help bring about an age of peace, he remonstrated firmly on every issue.

sentences.zh: 錢寧、江彬雖伏誅，而張銳、張忠、於經、許泰等獄久不決。

translations.literal: Although Qian Ning and Jiang Bin had been executed, the cases of Zhang Rui, Zhang Zhong, Yu Jing, Xu Tai, and others long remained undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Although Qian Ning and Jiang Bin had been put to death, the cases of Zhang Rui, Zhang Zhong, Yu Jing, Xu Tai, and others dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 廷和等言：「不誅此曹，則國法不正，公道不明，九廟之靈不安，萬姓之心不服，禍亂之機未息，太平之治未臻。」

translations.literal: Tinghe and the others said, "If these men are not executed, then state law will not be upright, public justice will not be clear, the spirits of the nine temples will not rest, the hearts of the myriad people will not be satisfied, the seeds of calamity and rebellion will not be stilled, and the governance of great peace will not be attained.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe and his colleagues said, "If these men are not executed, state law will not stand upright, public justice will remain clouded, the spirits of the imperial ancestors will not rest, the people will not be satisfied, the seeds of rebellion will not be uprooted, and true peace will not be achieved.

sentences.zh: 帝乃籍沒其資產。

translations.literal: The emperor then confiscated their property.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered their assets confiscated.

sentences.zh: 廷和復疏請敬天戒，法祖訓，隆孝道，保聖躬，務民義，勤學問，慎命令，明賞罰，專委任，納諫諍，親善人，節財用。

translations.literal: Tinghe again memorialized requesting that the emperor revere Heaven and be cautious, follow ancestral instruction, exalt filial piety, preserve the sacred person, attend to the people's righteousness, be diligent in study, be careful in commands, clarify rewards and punishments, delegate authority exclusively, accept remonstrance, be close to good men, and economize expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe again memorialized urging the emperor to revere Heaven and be vigilant, follow ancestral instruction, exalt filial piety, preserve his health, serve the people's welfare, study diligently, issue commands carefully, make rewards and punishments clear, delegate authority resolutely, accept remonstrance, keep company with good men, and restrain expenditure.

sentences.zh: 語多剴切，皆優詔報可。

translations.literal: His words were many and incisive, and all were answered with gracious edicts of approval.
translations.idiomatic: His language was forthright and searching, and in every case the emperor replied with gracious edicts of approval.

sentences.zh: 及議「大禮」，廷和持論益不撓，卒以是忤帝意。

translations.literal: When the "Great Rites" were debated, Tinghe held to his position ever more unyieldingly and ultimately thereby offended the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Rites controversy arose, Tinghe held his ground ever more firmly and ultimately offended the emperor.

sentences.zh: 先是，武宗崩，廷和草遺詔。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Wuzong died, Tinghe drafted the testamentary edict.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Wuzong died, Tinghe drafted the testamentary edict.

sentences.zh: 言皇考孝宗敬皇帝親弟興獻王長子某，倫序當立。

translations.literal: It stated that a certain person, eldest son of the Prince of Xing, younger brother by birth of the late Emperor Xiaozong, should succeed by order of precedence.
translations.idiomatic: It stated that the eldest son of the Prince of Xing, the late Emperor Xiaozong's younger brother by birth, should succeed by right of precedence.

sentences.zh: 遵奉《祖訓》兄終弟及之文，告於宗廟，請於慈壽皇太后，迎嗣皇帝位。

translations.literal: Following the text in the Ancestral Instructions on an elder brother's death and a younger brother's succession, it reported to the ancestral temples, requested permission of Empress Dowager Cishou, and welcomed him to succeed to the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: Invoking the Ancestral Instructions on succession when an elder brother dies without an heir, it reported to the ancestral temples, sought the approval of Empress Dowager Cishou, and welcomed him to the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 既令禮官上禮儀狀，請由東安門入居文華殿。

translations.literal: It then ordered the ritual officials to submit a protocol requesting that he enter through the East Gate and take up residence in the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: It then ordered the ritual officials to submit a protocol proposing that he enter through the East Gate and take up residence in the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 翼日，百官三上箋勸進，俟令旨俞允，擇日即位。

translations.literal: The next day the hundred officials thrice submitted memorials urging accession; awaiting the order of approval, a day was chosen for enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the officials submitted memorials urging accession three times; once imperial approval was granted, a date was chosen for enthronement.

sentences.zh: 其箋文皆循皇子嗣位故事。

translations.literal: The texts of their memorials all followed the precedent for a prince succeeding to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials all followed the precedent for a prince succeeding to the throne.

sentences.zh: 世宗覽禮部狀，謂：「遺詔以吾嗣皇帝位，非為皇子也。」

translations.literal: When Shizong read the Ministry of Rites protocol, he said, "The testamentary edict installs me as successor to the imperial throne; it is not making me a prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Shizong read the Ministry of Rites protocol, he said, "The testamentary edict makes me successor to the imperial throne; it is not treating me as a prince.

sentences.zh: 及至京，止城外。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, he stopped outside the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital, he halted outside the city walls.

sentences.zh: 廷和固請如禮部所具儀，世宗不聽。

translations.literal: Tinghe firmly requested that matters proceed according to the ritual prepared by the Ministry of Rites; Shizong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe firmly insisted on the ritual prepared by the Ministry of Rites; the future emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 乃御行殿受箋，由大明門直入，告大行几筵，日中即帝位。

translations.literal: He thereupon received the memorials at the traveling hall, entered directly through the Great Ming Gate, reported before the late emperor's spirit table, and at noon took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He then received the memorials at the traveling hall, entered directly through the Great Ming Gate, announced himself before the late emperor's spirit tablet, and took the throne at noon.

sentences.zh: 詔草言「奉皇兄遺詔入奉宗祧」，帝遲回久之，始報可。

translations.literal: The draft edict said that he was "following the late imperial brother's testamentary edict to enter and serve the ancestral line"; the emperor deliberated for a long time before at last approving it.
translations.idiomatic: The draft edict said that he was "following his late imperial brother's testamentary edict to enter and serve the ancestral line"; the emperor hesitated for a long time before finally approving it.

sentences.zh: 越三日，遣官往迎帝母興獻妃。

translations.literal: Three days later he dispatched officials to welcome the emperor's mother, Princess Consort of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later he dispatched officials to welcome his mother, the Princess Consort of Xing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，命禮官議興獻王主祀稱號。

translations.literal: Before long he ordered the ritual officials to deliberate the sacrificial rites and titles of the Prince of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he ordered the ritual officials to deliberate the sacrificial rites and titles due to the Prince of Xing.

sentences.zh: 廷和檢漢定陶王、宋濮王事授尚書毛澄曰：「是足為據，宜尊孝宗曰『皇考』，稱獻王為『皇叔考興國大王』，母妃為『皇叔母興國太妃』，自稱『侄皇帝』名，別立益王次子崇仁王為興王，奉獻王祀。

translations.literal: Tinghe examined the cases of the Han Prince of Dingtao and the Song Prince of Pu and handed them to Minister Mao Cheng, saying, "These suffice as precedent. Xiaozong should be honored as 'Imperial Father'; the Prince of Xing should be styled 'Imperial Uncle Father, King of Xing'; his consort as 'Imperial Uncle Mother, Grand Princess of Xing'; the emperor should style himself 'Nephew Emperor'; and the second son of the Prince of Yi, the Prince of Chongren, should separately be established as Prince of Xing to perform the Prince of Xing's sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe reviewed the cases of the Han Prince of Dingtao and the Song Prince of Pu and gave them to Minister Mao Cheng, saying, "These are sufficient precedent. Xiaozong should be honored as 'Imperial Father'; the Prince of Xing should be styled 'Imperial Uncle Father, King of Xing'; his consort as 'Imperial Uncle Mother, Grand Princess of Xing'; the emperor should style himself 'Nephew Emperor'; and the Prince of Yi's second son, the Prince of Chongren, should be established separately as Prince of Xing to maintain the Prince of Xing's sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 有異議者即奸邪，當斬。」

translations.literal: Whoever raises a different view is treacherous and should be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who disagrees is a traitor and should be put to death.

sentences.zh: 進士張璁與侍郎王瓚言，帝入繼大統，非為人後。

translations.literal: Presented Scholar Zhang Cong, together with Vice Minister Wang Zan, argued that in succeeding to the grand line the emperor was not succeeding as someone else's heir.
translations.idiomatic: Presented Scholar Zhang Cong, together with Vice Minister Wang Zan, argued that in taking the throne the emperor was succeeding to the imperial line, not becoming another man's heir.

sentences.zh: 瓚微言之，廷和恐其撓議，改瓚官南京。

translations.literal: Zan hinted at this; Tinghe, fearing that he would disrupt the deliberation, transferred Zan to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zan hinted at this view; fearing that he would disrupt the debate, Tinghe transferred him to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 五月，澄會廷臣議上，如廷和言。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Cheng convened the court ministers and submitted their deliberation, in accordance with Tinghe's words.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Mao Cheng convened the court ministers and submitted their recommendation, following Tinghe's position.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 然每召廷和從容賜茶慰諭，欲有所更定，廷和卒不肯順帝指。

translations.literal: Yet each time he summoned Tinghe, he graciously offered tea and consoled him, wishing to make changes; Tinghe ultimately would not follow the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet each time he summoned Tinghe he offered tea and spoke reassuringly, hoping to secure changes; Tinghe ultimately refused to yield to the emperor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 乃下廷臣再議。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered the court ministers to deliberate again.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the court ministers to deliberate again.

sentences.zh: 廷和偕蔣冕、毛紀奏言：「前代入繼之君，追崇所生者，皆不合典禮。

translations.literal: Tinghe, together with Jiang Mian and Mao Ji, memorialized, saying, "Emperors of previous generations who succeeded by adoption and posthumously honored their biological parents all did so in violation of ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe, together with Jiang Mian and Mao Ji, memorialized, saying, "Previous emperors who succeeded by adoption and then posthumously honored their biological parents all violated proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 惟宋儒程頤《濮議》最得義理之正，可為萬世法。

translations.literal: Only the Song Confucian Cheng Yi's 'Debate on the Prince of Pu' most fully attains the correctness of principle and may serve as law for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Song Confucian Cheng Yi's Debate on the Prince of Pu most fully captures the right principle and may serve as a model for all ages.

sentences.zh: 至興獻王祀，雖崇仁王主之，他日皇嗣繁衍，仍以第二子為興獻王後，而改封崇仁王為親王，則天理人情，兩全無失。」

translations.literal: As for the sacrifices to the Prince of Xing, although the Prince of Chongren would preside over them, when the imperial heirs multiply in future days the second son should still be made heir to the Prince of Xing, while the Prince of Chongren would be re-enfeoffed as a prince of the blood; then heavenly principle and human sentiment would both be fulfilled without loss.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Prince of Xing's sacrifices, although the Prince of Chongren would preside over them, when imperial heirs multiply in the future the second son should still succeed as heir to the Prince of Xing, while the Prince of Chongren would be re-enfeoffed as a prince of the blood; in that way principle and human feeling would both be satisfied.

sentences.zh: 帝益不悅，命博考典禮，務求至當。

translations.literal: The emperor was increasingly displeased and ordered a broad examination of ritual texts, striving for what was most appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still more displeased and ordered a wide review of ritual precedents, insisting on a fully satisfactory solution.

sentences.zh: 廷和、冕、紀復言：「三代以前，聖莫如舜，未聞追崇其所生父瞽瞍也。

translations.literal: Tinghe, Mian, and Ji again said, "Before the Three Dynasties, none was more sage than Shun, yet one never hears of his posthumously honoring his biological father Gusou.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe, Jiang Mian, and Mao Ji replied again, "Before the Three Dynasties, none was more sage than Shun, yet he never posthumously honored his biological father Gusou.

sentences.zh: 三代以後，賢莫如漢光武，未聞追崇其所生父南頓君也。

translations.literal: After the Three Dynasties, none was more worthy than Han Guangwu, yet one never hears of his posthumously honoring his biological father, the Lord of Nandun.
translations.idiomatic: After the Three Dynasties, none was more worthy than Emperor Guangwu of Han, yet he never posthumously honored his biological father, the Lord of Nandun.

sentences.zh: 惟皇上取法二君，則聖德無累，聖孝有光矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty takes these two rulers as your model, then your sagely virtue will be unblemished and your sagely filial piety will shine forth.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty takes these two rulers as your model, your sagely virtue will remain untarnished and your filial piety will shine all the brighter.

sentences.zh: 澄等亦再三執奏。

translations.literal: Cheng and the others also repeatedly held firm in memorializing.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Cheng and the others also repeatedly submitted firm memorials.

sentences.zh: 帝留中不下。

translations.literal: The emperor retained the memorials at court without issuing a reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept the memorials at court and issued no reply.

sentences.zh: 七月，張璁上疏謂當繼統，不繼嗣。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Zhang Cong memorialized that one should succeed to the line, not to an heirship.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Zhang Cong memorialized that the emperor should succeed to the imperial line, not to another's heirship.

sentences.zh: 帝遣司禮太監持示廷和，言此議遵祖訓，據古禮，宜從。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a grand eunuch of the Directorate to show it to Tinghe, saying that this proposal followed the ancestral instructions and ancient rites and should be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a grand eunuch of the Directorate to show the memorial to Tinghe, saying that this proposal followed the ancestral instructions and ancient rites and ought to be accepted.

sentences.zh: 廷和曰「秀才安知國家事體」，復持入。

translations.literal: Tinghe said, "What does a presented scholar know of the affairs of state?" and returned it inside.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe said, "What does a newly minted scholar know about affairs of state?" and sent it back.

sentences.zh: 無何，帝御文華殿召廷和、冕、紀，授以手敕，令尊父母為帝、后。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor held court at the Wenhua Hall, summoned Tinghe, Mian, and Ji, and handed them a sealed edict ordering that his parents be honored as emperor and empress.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor held court at the Wenhua Hall, summoned Tinghe, Jiang Mian, and Mao Ji, and handed them a sealed edict ordering that his parents be honored as emperor and empress.

sentences.zh: 廷和退而上奏曰：「《禮》謂為所後者為父母，而以其所生者為伯叔父母，蓋不惟降其服而又異其名也。

translations.literal: Tinghe withdrew and memorialized, saying, "The Rites state that one's parents are those to whom one succeeds, and one's biological parents are treated as uncle and aunt; this not only lowers the mourning garments but also changes their titles.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe withdrew and memorialized, saying, "The Rites teach that one's parents are those to whom one succeeds, while one's biological parents are treated as uncle and aunt; this not only lowers the mourning garments but also changes their titles.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢阿諛順旨。」

translations.literal: Your servant dares not flatter and follow the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant dares not flatter the throne and simply obey.

sentences.zh: 仍封還手詔。

translations.literal: He still returned the sealed edict sealed.
translations.idiomatic: He returned the sealed edict unopened.

sentences.zh: 群臣亦皆執前議。

translations.literal: The ministers also all held to the previous deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The other ministers also held to their earlier position.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 迨九月，母妃至京，帝自定儀由中門入，謁見太廟，復申諭欲加稱興獻帝、后為「皇」。

translations.literal: By the ninth month, when his mother the consort reached the capital, the emperor himself set the ritual for her entry through the middle gate and audience at the Imperial Ancestral Temple; he again announced his wish to add the designation "Imperial" to the Prince of Xing as emperor and empress.
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth month, when his mother reached the capital, the emperor himself prescribed the ritual for her entry through the middle gate and her audience at the Imperial Ancestral Temple; he again declared his wish to add the designation "Imperial" to his father and mother, the Prince of Xing and his consort.

sentences.zh: 廷和言：「漢宣帝繼孝昭後，謚史皇孫、王夫人曰悼考、悼后，光武上繼元帝，鉅鹿、南頓君以上立廟章陵，皆未嘗追尊。

translations.literal: Tinghe said, "When Han Emperor Xuandi succeeded after Emperor Xiaozhao of Han, he gave the posthumous titles Mourning Father and Mourning Mother to Emperor Shihuangsun and Lady Wang; when Guangwu succeeded after Emperor Yuandi, he erected temples at Zhangling for the Lord of Julu, the Lord of Nandun, and those above them—yet none of these cases involved posthumous elevation.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe said, "When Emperor Xuandi of Han succeeded after Emperor Xiaozhao, he gave the posthumous titles Mourning Father and Mourning Mother to Emperor Shihuangsun and Lady Wang; when Guangwu succeeded after Emperor Yuandi, he erected temples at Zhangling for the Lord of Julu, the Lord of Nandun, and their forebears—yet in none of these cases was there posthumous elevation.

sentences.zh: 今若加皇字，與孝廟、慈壽並，是忘所後而重本生，任私恩而棄大義，臣等不得辭其責。」

translations.literal: If today the character 'Imperial' is added, putting them on a par with the Xiaozong temple and Cishou, that is forgetting whom one has succeeded and overweighting one's biological origins, indulging private favor and abandoning great righteousness; we ministers cannot shirk our responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: If the title 'Imperial' is added now, placing them on a par with Xiaozong's temple and Empress Dowager Cishou, that means forgetting the line one has succeeded and exalting one's biological parents over public duty, indulging private feeling at the expense of great principle; we ministers cannot escape blame.

sentences.zh: 因自請斥罷。

translations.literal: He thereupon requested his own dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon asked to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 廷臣諍者百余人。

translations.literal: More than a hundred court ministers remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred court ministers remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，乃以嘉靖元年詔稱孝宗為「皇考」，慈壽皇太后為「聖母」，興獻帝、后為本生父母，不稱「皇」。

translations.literal: The emperor, having no alternative, then by an edict of the first year of Jiajing styled Xiaozong as "Imperial Father," Empress Dowager Cishou as "Holy Mother," and the Prince of Xing and his consort as biological parents, without the designation "Imperial."
translations.idiomatic: Left with no alternative, the emperor issued an edict in the first year of Jiajing styling Xiaozong as "Imperial Father," Empress Dowager Cishou as "Holy Mother," and the Prince of Xing and his consort as biological parents without the designation "Imperial."

sentences.zh: 當是時，廷和先後封還御批者四，執奏幾三十疏，帝常忽忽有所恨。

translations.literal: At that time Tinghe had successively returned four imperial rescripts sealed and had submitted nearly thirty firm memorials; the emperor often harbored vague resentment.
translations.idiomatic: By then Tinghe had returned four imperial rescripts unopened and submitted nearly thirty firm memorials; the emperor often nursed a brooding resentment.

sentences.zh: 左右因乘間言廷和恣無人臣禮。

translations.literal: Those around him therefore seized the opportunity to say that Tinghe acted willfully without a minister's propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Those around the emperor therefore took the opportunity to say that Tinghe had grown willful and lacked a subject's proper deference.

sentences.zh: 言官史道、曹嘉遂交劾廷和。

translations.literal: The remonstrance officials Shi Dao and Cao Jia then submitted memorial after memorial impeaching Tinghe.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrance officials Shi Dao and Cao Jia then submitted memorial after memorial impeaching Tinghe.

sentences.zh: 帝為薄謫道、嘉以安廷和，然意內移矣。

translations.literal: The emperor lightly demoted Dao and Jia to reassure Tinghe, yet inwardly his mind had already shifted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lightly punished Dao and Jia to reassure Tinghe, but inwardly his sympathies had already shifted.

sentences.zh: 尋論定策功，封廷和、冕、紀伯爵，歲祿千石，廷和固辭。

translations.literal: Soon, when merit in settling the succession was deliberated, Tinghe, Mian, and Ji were enfeoffed as earls with stipends of a thousand shi; Tinghe firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when rewards were granted for settling the succession, Tinghe, Jiang Mian, and Mao Ji were enfeoffed as earls with stipends of a thousand shi; Tinghe firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 改蔭錦衣衛指揮使，復辭。

translations.literal: It was changed to hereditary commandership in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard; he again declined.
translations.idiomatic: The reward was changed to a hereditary commandership in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard; he declined again.

sentences.zh: 帝以賞太輕，加蔭四品京職世襲，復辭。

translations.literal: The emperor thought the reward too light and added a hereditary fourth-rank capital office; he again declined.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought the reward too modest and added a hereditary fourth-rank capital office; Tinghe declined again.

sentences.zh: 會滿四考，超拜太傅，復四辭而止。

translations.literal: When his four appraisals were completed he was promoted over the regular sequence to Grand Preceptor; after four refusals he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When his four appraisals were complete he was promoted out of turn to Grand Preceptor; he declined four times and then accepted.

sentences.zh: 特賜敕旌異，錫宴於禮部，九卿皆與焉。

translations.literal: He was specially granted an edict of exceptional commendation and a banquet at the Ministry of Rites, with all nine ministers in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially granted an edict of exceptional commendation and a banquet at the Ministry of Rites attended by all nine ministers.

sentences.zh: 廷和先累疏乞休，其後請益力。

translations.literal: Tinghe had earlier submitted memorial after memorial begging to retire, and afterward his requests grew more forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe had already submitted repeated memorials asking to retire, and his requests grew ever more urgent.

sentences.zh: 又以持考獻帝議不合，疏語露不平。

translations.literal: Also, because his insistence in the debate over honoring his biological father as emperor did not accord with the emperor's view, the language of his memorials revealed discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, because his stubborn stand in the debate over honoring the emperor's biological father did not accord with the throne's wishes, the tone of his memorials betrayed his resentment.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，帝聽之去。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, the emperor granted his request to leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, the emperor allowed him to retire.

sentences.zh: 責以因辭歸咎，非大臣道。

translations.literal: He was rebuked for shifting blame through his language of resignation—this was not the way of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was rebuked for using his resignation to shift blame—conduct unbecoming a great minister.

sentences.zh: 然猶賜璽書，給輿廩郵護如例，申前蔭子錦衣衛指揮使之命。

translations.literal: Yet he was still granted an imperial letter with the seal, given carriage, stipends, and postal escort according to precedent, and the earlier command conferring hereditary commandership in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard on his son was reaffirmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still received an imperial letter under seal, carriage, stipends, and postal escort as usual, and the earlier appointment of his son as hereditary commandant of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard was confirmed.

sentences.zh: 給事、御史請留廷和，皆不報。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries and censors requested that Tinghe be retained; none received a reply.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries and censors asked that Tinghe be kept in office; the throne issued no reply.

sentences.zh: 廷和去，始議稱孝宗為「皇伯考」。

translations.literal: After Tinghe departed, deliberations began to style Xiaozong as "Imperial Uncle-Father."
translations.idiomatic: Only after Tinghe left did deliberations begin to style Emperor Xiaozong as "Imperial Uncle-Father."

sentences.zh: 於是，廷和子修撰慎率群臣伏闕哭爭，杖謫雲南。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tinghe's son, Hanlin Reviser Shen, led the officials in weeping and remonstrating at the palace gate; they were beaten with the rod and exiled to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Tinghe's son, Hanlin Reviser Yang Shen, led the officials in kneeling at the palace gate to weep and remonstrate; they were beaten with the rod and banished to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 既而王邦奇誣訐廷和及其次子兵部主事惇、婿修撰金承勛、鄉人侍讀葉桂章與彭澤弟沖交關請屬，俱逮下詔獄。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Wang Bangqi falsely accused Tinghe, his second son Dun who was a principal secretary in the Ministry of War, his son-in-law Hanlin Reviser Jin Chengxun, his fellow townsman Hanlin Reader Ye Guizhang, and Peng Ze's younger brother Chong of improper connections and seeking favors; all were arrested and sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Wang Bangqi falsely accused Tinghe, his second son Dun of the Ministry of War, his son-in-law Hanlin Reviser Jin Chengxun, his fellow townsman Hanlin Reader Ye Guizhang, and Peng Ze's younger brother Chong of corrupt dealings and soliciting favors; all were arrested and sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 鞫治無狀，乃得解。

translations.literal: Investigation found no substance to the charges, and they were released.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation found no basis for the charges, and they were released.

sentences.zh: 七年，《明倫大典》成，詔定議禮諸臣罪。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the Minglun Dadian was completed, an edict was issued to fix the offenses of the officials who had deliberated on the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when the Minglun Dadian was completed, an edict fixed the offenses of the officials who had deliberated on the rites.

sentences.zh: 言廷和謬主《濮議》，自詭門生天子、定策國老，法當僇市，姑削職為民。

translations.literal: It stated that Tinghe had wrongly upheld the Puyi precedent, falsely styled himself the emperor's teacher and the elder statesman who settled policy; by law he deserved execution at the market, but for the present his office was stripped and he was made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: It charged that Tinghe had wrongly upheld the Puyi precedent, falsely styling himself the emperor's teacher and the elder statesman who settled the succession; by law he deserved execution at the market, but for the present his office was stripped and he was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 明年六月卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: The following year, in the sixth month, he died at the age of seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the sixth month, he died at seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 居久之，帝問大學士李時：「太倉所積幾何？」

translations.literal: After some time had passed, the emperor asked Grand Secretary Li Shi: "How much grain is stored at Taicang?
translations.idiomatic: After some time, the emperor asked Grand Secretary Li Shi, "How much grain is stored at Taicang?

sentences.zh: 時對曰：「可支數年。

translations.literal: Li Shi replied: "It can supply several years.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi replied, "It can supply several years.

sentences.zh: 由陛下初年詔書裁革冗員所致。」

translations.literal: This is owing to the edicts in Your Majesty's early reign cutting redundant personnel."
translations.idiomatic: This is owing to the edicts in Your Majesty's early reign cutting redundant personnel."

sentences.zh: 帝慨然曰：「此楊廷和功，不可沒也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said with emotion: "This was Yang Tinghe's achievement; it must not be erased."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with feeling, "This was Yang Tinghe's achievement; it must not be forgotten."

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，復官，贈太保，謚文忠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was restored to office posthumously, granted the posthumous title Grand Preceptor, and given the posthumous name Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longqing his office was posthumously restored, he was granted the title Grand Preceptor, and given the posthumous name Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 初，廷和入閣，東陽謂曰：「吾於文翰，頗有一日之長，若經濟事須歸介夫。」

translations.literal: Early on, when Tinghe entered the Grand Secretariat, Dong Yang said to him: "In literary matters I am somewhat better, but in statecraft affairs one must defer to Jiefu.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, when Tinghe entered the Grand Secretariat, Dong Yang told him, "In literary matters I have some advantage, but in statecraft one must defer to Jiefu.

sentences.zh: 及武宗之終，卒安社稷者，廷和力也，人以東陽為知言。

translations.literal: When the Wuzong reign ended, it was Tinghe's effort that ultimately stabilized the realm; people regarded Dong Yang as having spoken truly.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong's reign ended, it was Tinghe's effort that ultimately stabilized the realm; people regarded Dong Yang as having spoken truly.

sentences.zh: 弟廷儀，兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: His younger brother Tingyi was Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Tingyi was Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 子慎、惇，孫有仁，皆進士。

translations.literal: His sons Shen and Dun and his grandson Youren all became jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Shen and Dun and his grandson Youren all passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 慎自有傳。

translations.literal: Shen has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shen has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 梁儲，字叔厚，廣東順德人。

translations.literal: Liang Chu, styled Shuhou, was a man of Shunde in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chu, styled Shuhou, was from Shunde in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 受業陳獻章。

translations.literal: He studied under Chen Xianzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Chen Xianzhang.

sentences.zh: 舉成化十四年會試第一，選庶吉士，授編修，尋兼司經局校書。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chenghua he ranked first in the metropolitan examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed reviser, and soon also served as collator in the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 14 he ranked first in the metropolitan examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed reviser, and soon also served as collator in the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年，進侍講。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi he was promoted to Hanlin expositor.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 4 he was promoted to Hanlin expositor.

sentences.zh: 改洗馬，侍武宗於東宮。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as junior tutor and attended the future Wuzong in the Eastern Palace.
