translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as junior tutor and attended the future Emperor Wuzong in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 冊封安南，卻其饋。

translations.literal: When invested to ennoble Annan, he declined its gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When sent to invest the ruler of Annan, he declined the gifts offered him.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢翰林學士，同修《會典》，遷少詹事，拜吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: After some time he was promoted to Hanlin academician, helped compile the Huidian, was transferred to junior tutor of the heir apparent, and appointed Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to Hanlin academician, helped compile the Huidian, was made junior tutor of the heir apparent, and appointed Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 正德初，改左，進尚書，專典誥敕，掌詹事府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he was moved to the left side, promoted to minister, and was put in charge of drafting edicts of appointment and administering the Directorate of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengde reign he was moved to the left, promoted to minister, put in charge of drafting edicts of appointment, and made head of the Directorate of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾摘《會典》小疵，儲坐降右侍郎。

translations.literal: Liu Jin seized on minor flaws in the Huidian, and Chu was demoted to vice minister on the right for it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin seized on minor flaws in the Huidian, and Chu was demoted to vice minister on the right.

sentences.zh: 《孝宗實錄》成，復尚書，尋加太子少保，調南京吏部。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Xiaozong were completed, he was restored as minister; soon he was added as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of Emperor Xiaozong were completed, he was restored as minister; soon he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，以吏部尚書兼文淵閣大學士，入參機務。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed, he served as Minister of Personnel concurrently with Grand Secretary in the Wenyuan Pavilion and entered to deliberate on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, he served as Minister of Personnel concurrently with Grand Secretary in the Wenyuan Pavilion and entered to deliberate on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 屢加少傅、太子太傅，進建極殿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly elevated to Junior Mentor, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and entered the Jianji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly elevated to Junior Mentor and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and entered the Jianji Hall.

sentences.zh: 十年，楊廷和遭喪去，儲為首輔。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when Yang Tinghe left for mourning, Chu became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when Yang Tinghe left for mourning, Chu became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 進少師、太子太師、華蓋殿大學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Junior Preceptor, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and Grand Secretary in the Huagai Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Preceptor, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and Grand Secretary in the Huagai Hall.

sentences.zh: 時方建乾清、坤寧宮，又營太素殿、天鵝房、船塢，儲偕同官靳貴、楊一清切諫。

translations.literal: At that time the Qianqing and Kunning palaces were being built, and the Taisu Hall, swan enclosure, and shipyard were also under construction; Chu together with his colleagues Jin Gui and Yang Yiqing remonstrated urgently.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Qianqing and Kunning palaces were being built, along with the Taisu Hall, swan enclosure, and shipyard; Chu together with Jin Gui and Yang Yiqing remonstrated urgently.

sentences.zh: 明年春，以國本未定，請擇宗室賢者居京師，備儲貳之選，皆不報。

translations.literal: The next spring, because the foundation of the state had not been settled, he requested that talented members of the imperial clan be selected to reside in the capital as candidates for the heir; none received a reply.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring, because no heir had been designated, he asked that talented members of the imperial clan be brought to the capital as candidates for the succession; the throne issued no reply.

sentences.zh: 其秋，一清罷，蔣冕代之。

translations.literal: That autumn Yang Yiqing was dismissed and Jiang Mian replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Yang Yiqing was dismissed and Jiang Mian replaced him.

sentences.zh: 至明年，貴亦罷，毛紀入閣。

translations.literal: By the following year Jin Gui was also dismissed and Mao Ji entered the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: By the following year Jin Gui was also dismissed and Mao Ji entered the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝好微行，嘗出西安門，經宿返。

translations.literal: The emperor liked to travel incognito; once he went out through Xi'an Gate and returned after spending the night away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor liked to travel incognito; once he went out through Xi'an Gate and did not return until the next day.

sentences.zh: 儲等諫，不聽，然猶慮外廷知。

translations.literal: Chu and the others remonstrated, but the emperor would not listen; yet he still feared that the outer court would learn of it.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and the others remonstrated, but the emperor would not listen; yet he still feared that the outer court would learn of it.

sentences.zh: 是春，從近幸言召百官至左順門，明告以郊祀畢，幸南海子觀獵。

translations.literal: That spring, following advice from his close attendants, he summoned all officials to Zuoshun Gate and openly announced that after the suburban sacrifice he would visit the Southern Park to watch the hunt.
translations.idiomatic: That spring, on the advice of his close attendants, he summoned all officials to Zuoshun Gate and openly announced that after the suburban sacrifice he would visit the Southern Park to watch the hunt.

sentences.zh: 儲等暨廷臣諫，皆不納。

translations.literal: Chu and the others, together with the court officials, remonstrated; none of it was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and the others, together with the court officials, remonstrated; none of it was heeded.

sentences.zh: 八月朔，微服從數十騎幸昌平。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eighth month, in plain dress and with several dozen horsemen, he visited Changping.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eighth month, in plain dress and with several dozen horsemen, he visited Changping.

sentences.zh: 次日，儲、冕、紀始覺，追至沙河不及，連疏請回鑾。

translations.literal: The next day Chu, Mian, and Ji became aware of it, pursued him as far as Shahe but could not catch up, and submitted memorial after memorial asking him to return.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Chu, Jiang Mian, and Mao Ji learned of it, pursued him as far as Shahe but could not catch up, and submitted memorial after memorial asking him to return.

sentences.zh: 越十有三日乃旋。

translations.literal: It was more than thirteen days before he returned.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirteen days passed before he returned.

sentences.zh: 儲等以國無儲副，而帝盤遊不息，中外危疑，力申建儲之請，亦不報。

translations.literal: Chu and the others, because the state had no heir apparent and the emperor's roaming amusements never ceased, said the court and realm were filled with alarm and doubt, and urgently renewed their request to establish an heir; again no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and the others, because the state had no heir apparent and the emperor's roaming amusements never ceased, said alarm and doubt filled court and realm, and urgently renewed their request to establish an heir; again there was no reply.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝馳出居庸關，幸宣府，命谷大用守關，無縱廷臣出。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the emperor galloped out through Juyong Pass and visited Xuanfu; he ordered Gu Dayong to hold the pass and not let court officials out.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the emperor galloped out through Juyong Pass to Xuanfu; he ordered Gu Dayong to hold the pass and not let court officials through.

sentences.zh: 遂由宣府抵大同，遇寇於應州，幾殆。

translations.literal: He then went from Xuanfu to Datong and encountered bandits at Yingzhou, nearly losing his life.
translations.idiomatic: He then went from Xuanfu to Datong and encountered bandits at Yingzhou, nearly losing his life.

sentences.zh: 儲等憂懼，請回鑾益急。

translations.literal: Chu and the others were anxious and fearful and pressed ever more urgently for his return.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and the others were filled with alarm and pressed ever more urgently for his return.

sentences.zh: 章十余上，帝不為動，歲除竟駐宣府。

translations.literal: More than ten memorials were submitted; the emperor was unmoved, and at year's end he was still lodged at Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten memorials were submitted; the emperor was unmoved, and at year's end he was still lodged at Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝失德彌甚。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor's misdeeds grew ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor's misconduct grew ever worse.

sentences.zh: 群小竊權，濁亂朝政，人情惶惶。

translations.literal: Petty men usurped power, the governance was muddied and disordered, and public sentiment was terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men usurped power, governance was corrupted and disordered, and public sentiment was terrified.

sentences.zh: 儲懼不克任，以廷和服闋，屢請召之。

translations.literal: Chu feared he could not bear the burden; as Tinghe's mourning period had ended, he repeatedly asked that Tinghe be summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Chu feared he could not bear the burden; as Tinghe's mourning period had ended, he repeatedly asked that Tinghe be summoned back.

sentences.zh: 廷和還朝，儲遂讓而處其下。

translations.literal: When Tinghe returned to court, Chu yielded and placed himself below him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tinghe returned to court, Chu yielded and placed himself below him.

sentences.zh: 鳳陽守備中官丘德及鎮守延綏、寧夏、大同、宣府諸中官皆乞更敕書兼理民事，帝許之。

translations.literal: The eunuch Qiu De, garrison commander at Fengyang, and the eunuchs garrisoning Yan-sui, Ningxia, Datong, Xuanfu, and other posts all requested revised edicts to administer civil affairs as well; the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Qiu De, garrison commander at Fengyang, and the eunuchs garrisoning Yan-sui, Ningxia, Datong, Xuanfu, and other posts all requested revised edicts to administer civil affairs as well; the emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 儲等極言不可，弗聽。

translations.literal: Chu and the others spoke out strongly that this was impermissible; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and the others spoke out strongly against it; the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 十三年七月，帝從江彬言，將遍遊塞上。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the thirteenth year, following Jiang Bin's advice, the emperor planned to tour the entire northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the thirteenth year, following Jiang Bin's advice, the emperor planned to tour the entire northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 托言邊關多警，命總督軍務、威武大將軍、總兵官朱壽統六師往征，令內閣草敕。

translations.literal: On the pretext that the border posts were greatly alarmed, he ordered Zhu Shou, Grand Coordinator of Military Affairs, Awesome General, and regional commander, to lead the six armies on campaign, and commanded the Grand Secretariat to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: On the pretext that the border posts were greatly alarmed, he ordered Zhu Shou, Grand Coordinator of Military Affairs, Awesome General, and regional commander, to lead the six armies on campaign, and commanded the Grand Secretariat to draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 閣臣不可，帝復集百官左順門面諭。

translations.literal: The grand secretaries refused; the emperor then assembled the hundred officials at Zuoshun Gate and addressed them in person.
translations.idiomatic: The grand secretaries refused; the emperor then assembled the hundred officials at Zuoshun Gate and addressed them in person.

sentences.zh: 廷和、冕在告，儲、紀泣諫，眾亦泣，帝意不可回。

translations.literal: Tinghe and Mian were on leave for illness; Chu and Ji remonstrated through tears, the assembly wept as well, but the emperor's mind could not be turned.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe and Jiang Mian were on sick leave; Chu and Mao Ji remonstrated through tears, the assembly wept as well, but the emperor's mind could not be turned.

sentences.zh: 已而紀亦引疾。

translations.literal: Soon Mao Ji also pleaded illness and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Mao Ji also pleaded illness and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 儲獨廷爭累日，帝竟不聽。

translations.literal: Chu alone remonstrated at court for days on end, but in the end the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Chu alone remonstrated at court for days on end, but in the end the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 逾月，帝以「大將軍壽」肅清邊境，令加封「鎮國公」。

translations.literal: A month later, citing the "Great General Shou's" pacification of the frontier, he ordered that he be additionally enfeoffed as Duke Who Stabilizes the State.
translations.idiomatic: A month later, citing the "Great General Shou's" pacification of the frontier, he ordered that he be additionally enfeoffed as Duke Who Stabilizes the State.

sentences.zh: 儲、紀上言：「公雖貴，人臣耳。

translations.literal: Chu and Ji memorialized: "A duke, however exalted, is still only a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and Mao Ji memorialized, "A duke, however exalted, is still only a subject.

sentences.zh: 陛下承祖宗業，為天下君，奈何謬自貶損。

translations.literal: Your Majesty inherits the work of the ancestral temple and is sovereign of all under Heaven—why wrongly demean yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty inherits the work of the ancestral temple and is sovereign of all under Heaven—why demean yourself?

sentences.zh: 既封國公，則將授以誥券，追封三代。

translations.literal: Once enfeoffed as State Duke, he will be given an iron certificate and his three generations of ancestors will receive posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: Once enfeoffed as State Duke, he will be given an iron certificate and his three generations of ancestors will receive posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 祖宗在天之靈亦肯如陛下貶損否？

translations.literal: Would the ancestral spirits in Heaven consent to such demeaning as Your Majesty proposes?
translations.idiomatic: Would the ancestral spirits in Heaven consent to such demeaning as Your Majesty proposes?

sentences.zh: 況鐵券必有免死之文，陛下壽福無疆，何甘自菲薄，蒙此不祥之辭。

translations.literal: Moreover an iron certificate necessarily contains language granting exemption from death—Your Majesty's life and blessing are boundless; why willingly demean yourself with such ill-omened words?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover an iron certificate necessarily contains language granting exemption from death—Your Majesty's life and blessing are boundless; why willingly demean yourself with such ill-omened words?

sentences.zh: 名既不正，言自不順。

translations.literal: When the name is not correct, the words cannot be in order.
translations.idiomatic: When the name is not correct, the words cannot be in order.

sentences.zh: 臣等斷不敢阿意茍從，取他日戮身亡家之禍也。」

translations.literal: We dare not flatter and follow against our conscience, inviting the calamity of execution and the ruin of our families someday.
translations.idiomatic: We dare not flatter and follow against our conscience, inviting the calamity of execution and the ruin of our families.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply was issued.
translations.idiomatic: No reply was issued.

sentences.zh: 帝遂歷宣府、大同，直抵延綏。

translations.literal: The emperor then passed through Xuanfu and Datong and went straight to Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then passed through Xuanfu and Datong and went straight to Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 儲等疏數十上，悉置不省。

translations.literal: Chu and the others submitted dozens of memorials; all were set aside unread.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and the others submitted dozens of memorials; all were set aside unread.

sentences.zh: 秦王請關中閑田為牧地，江彬、錢寧、張忠等皆為之請。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin requested idle lands in Guanzhong as pasture; Jiang Bin, Qian Ning, Zhang Zhong, and others all pleaded on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin requested idle lands in Guanzhong as pasture; Jiang Bin, Qian Ning, Zhang Zhong, and others all pleaded on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 帝排群議許之，命閣臣草制。

translations.literal: The emperor brushed aside collective opposition and granted it, ordering the grand secretaries to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor brushed aside collective opposition and granted it, ordering the grand secretaries to draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 廷和、冕引疾，帝怒甚。

translations.literal: Tinghe and Mian pleaded illness; the emperor was furious.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe and Jiang Mian pleaded illness; the emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 儲度不可爭，乃上制草曰：「太祖高皇帝著令，茲土不畀藩封。

translations.literal: Chu judged the matter could not be contested, so he submitted a draft edict saying: "The founding emperor Gaozu issued an ordinance that these lands are not to be granted to feudal princes.
translations.idiomatic: Chu judged the matter could not be contested, so he submitted a draft edict saying, "The founding emperor Gaozu issued an ordinance that these lands are not to be granted to feudal princes.

sentences.zh: 非吝也，念其土廣饒，藩封得之，多蓄士馬，富而且驕，奸人誘為不軌，不利宗社。

translations.literal: It was not stinginess—he considered that the land is broad and fertile; if a feudal prince obtained it, he would gather many soldiers and horses, grow rich and arrogant, and wicked men would induce him toward disloyalty, to the detriment of the ancestral temple and state.
translations.idiomatic: It was not stinginess—he considered that the land is broad and fertile; if a feudal prince obtained it, he would gather many soldiers and horses, grow rich and arrogant, and wicked men would induce him toward disloyalty, to the detriment of the ancestral temple and state.

sentences.zh: 王今得地，宜益謹。

translations.literal: The prince now receiving this land should be all the more cautious.
translations.idiomatic: The prince now receiving this land should be all the more cautious.

sentences.zh: 毋收聚奸人，毋多蓄士馬，毋聽狂人謀不軌，震及邊方，危我社稷，是時雖欲保親親不可得已。」

translations.literal: Do not gather wicked men, do not amass many soldiers and horses, do not heed madmen plotting treason—if alarm reaches the borderlands and endangers our state, then even if he wishes to preserve kinship ties, it will be impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Do not gather wicked men, do not amass many soldiers and horses, do not heed madmen plotting treason—if alarm reaches the borderlands and endangers our state, then even if he wishes to preserve kinship ties, it will be impossible.

sentences.zh: 帝駭曰：「若是其可虞！」

translations.literal: The emperor was alarmed and said: "If so, this is greatly to be feared!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was alarmed and said, "If so, this is greatly to be feared!"

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝將南巡。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor planned to tour the south.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor planned to tour the south.

sentences.zh: 言官伏闕諫，儲、冕、紀亦以為言。

translations.literal: Censorial officials remonstrated kneeling at the palace gate; Chu, Mian, and Ji also spoke on it.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials remonstrated kneeling at the palace gate; Chu, Jiang Mian, and Mao Ji also spoke on it.

sentences.zh: 會諸曹多諫者，乃止。

translations.literal: As many offices joined in remonstrance, he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: As many offices joined in remonstrance, he stopped.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠反，帝南征，儲、冕扈從。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Ning Chenhao rebelled, the emperor marched south; Chu and Mian accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Ning Zhu Chenhao rebelled, the emperor marched south; Chu and Jiang Mian accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 在道聞賊滅，連疏請駕旋。

translations.literal: On the road he heard the rebel had been destroyed; memorial after memorial asked that the imperial carriage return.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he heard the rebel had been destroyed; memorial after memorial asked that the imperial carriage return.

sentences.zh: 抵揚州，帝議南京行郊禮。

translations.literal: Reaching Yangzhou, the emperor discussed performing the suburban rite at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Yangzhou, the emperor discussed performing the suburban rite at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 儲、冕計此議行，則回鑾益無日，極陳不可，疏三上始得請。

translations.literal: Chu and Mian calculated that if this proposal went forward, the return would be delayed indefinitely; they argued strongly against it, and only after three memorials did he consent.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and Jiang Mian calculated that if this proposal went forward, the return would be delayed indefinitely; they argued strongly against it, and only after three memorials did he consent.

sentences.zh: 帝以宸濠械將至，問處置之宜。

translations.literal: The emperor, since Chenhao in fetters was about to arrive, asked how he should be disposed of.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, since Chenhao in fetters was about to arrive, asked how he should be disposed of.

sentences.zh: 儲等請如宣宗征高煦故事，罪人既得，即日班師。

translations.literal: Chu and the others requested that it follow the precedent of Xuande's campaign against Gao Xu: once the culprit was taken, the army should withdraw the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and the others requested that it follow the precedent of the Xuande emperor's campaign against Gao Xu: once the culprit was taken, the army should withdraw the same day.

sentences.zh: 又因郊期改卜，四方災異、邊警，乞還乘輿。

translations.literal: They also cited the rescheduling of the suburban sacrifice, calamities and prodigies throughout the realm, and frontier alarms, begging that the imperial carriage return.
translations.idiomatic: They also cited the rescheduling of the suburban sacrifice, calamities and prodigies throughout the realm, and frontier alarms, begging that the imperial carriage return.

sentences.zh: 疏八九上，帝殊無還意。

translations.literal: Eight or nine memorials were submitted; the emperor showed not the least intention of returning.
translations.idiomatic: Eight or nine memorials were submitted; the emperor showed not the least intention of returning.

sentences.zh: 是秋，行在有物若豕首墮帝前，色碧，又進御婦人室中，若懸人首狀。

translations.literal: That autumn at the traveling palace something like a pig's head fell before the emperor, green in color; another appeared in the chamber of an imperial woman, shaped like a severed human head.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn at the traveling palace something like a pig's head fell before the emperor, green in color; another appeared in the chamber of an imperial woman, shaped like a severed human head.

sentences.zh: 人情益驚。

translations.literal: Public sentiment grew ever more alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Public sentiment grew ever more alarmed.

sentences.zh: 儲、冕危言諫，帝頗心動。

translations.literal: Chu and Mian remonstrated in the strongest terms; the emperor was somewhat moved.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and Jiang Mian remonstrated in the strongest terms; the emperor was somewhat moved.

sentences.zh: 而群小猶欲導帝遊浙西，泛江、漢。

translations.literal: Yet the petty men still wished to guide the emperor to tour western Zhejiang and sail the Yangzi and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the petty men still wished to guide the emperor to tour western Zhejiang and sail the Yangzi and Han.

sentences.zh: 儲、冕益懼，手疏跪泣行宮門外，歷未至酉。

translations.literal: Chu and Mian grew still more fearful; they wrote memorials by hand and, kneeling in tears outside the traveling palace gate, remained there until nearly the hour of you.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and Jiang Mian grew still more fearful; they wrote memorials by hand and, kneeling in tears outside the traveling palace gate, remained there until nearly the hour of you.

sentences.zh: 帝遣人取疏入，諭之起。

translations.literal: The emperor sent someone to take the memorials in and ordered them to rise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent someone to take the memorials in and ordered them to rise.

sentences.zh: 叩頭言：「未奉俞旨，不敢起也。」

translations.literal: He kowtowed and said, "Having not yet received the approving edict, I dare not rise."
translations.idiomatic: They kowtowed and said, "Without Your Majesty's approving edict, we dare not rise."

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，許不日還京，乃叩頭出。

translations.literal: The emperor, having no alternative, promised to return to the capital within a few days, and they kowtowed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, having no choice, promised to return to the capital within days, and they kowtowed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，楊廷和等定策迎興世子。

translations.literal: The emperor died; Yang Tinghe and others settled on a plan to welcome the heir of the Prince of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, Yang Tinghe and others settled on welcoming the heir of the Prince of Xing.

sentences.zh: 故事，當以內閣一人與中貴勛戚偕禮官往。

translations.literal: By precedent, one member of the Grand Secretariat should go together with palace eunuchs, meritorious kin, and ritual officials.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, one grand secretary was to go with palace eunuchs, ennobled kin, and ritual officials.

sentences.zh: 廷和欲留蔣冕自助，而慮儲老或憚行，乃佯惜儲憊老，阻其行。

translations.literal: Tinghe wished to retain Jiang Mian to assist himself, but feared that Chu, being old, might dread the journey, so he feigned pity for Chu's weariness and age and blocked his going.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghe wished to keep Jiang Mian at court to help him govern, but feared the elderly Chu might shrink from the journey, so he feigned concern that Chu was worn out and too old—and blocked his going.

sentences.zh: 儲奮曰：「事孰有大於此者，敢以憊辭！」

translations.literal: Chu exclaimed, "What affair is greater than this—how dare I plead weariness!
translations.idiomatic: Chu exclaimed, "What affair is greater than this? How dare I plead weariness!

sentences.zh: 遂與定國公徐光祚等迎世子安陸邸。

translations.literal: Thereupon, together with the Duke of Dingguo Xu Guangzuo and others, he went to welcome the heir at the Anlu residence.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon, together with the Duke of Dingguo Xu Guangzuo and others, he went to welcome the heir at the Anlu residence.

sentences.zh: 既即位，給事中張九敘等劾儲結納權奸，持祿固寵。

translations.literal: Once enthroned, Supervising Secretary Zhang Jiuxu and others impeached Chu for cultivating ties with powerful favorites and clinging to salary to preserve favor.
translations.idiomatic: After enthronement, Supervising Secretary Zhang Jiuxu and others impeached Chu for cultivating ties with powerful favorites and clinging to office to preserve influence.

sentences.zh: 儲三疏求去，命賜敕馳傳，遣行人護行，歲給廩隸如制。

translations.literal: Chu submitted three memorials asking to leave; he was ordered given an imperial letter with courier transport, escorted on the road by a palace attendant, with annual stipends and household servants according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Chu submitted three memorials asking to retire; the throne ordered an edict under seal with courier transport, a palace attendant to escort him homeward, and annual stipends and household servants as usual.

sentences.zh: 卒，子鈞奏請贈謚。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Jun memorialized requesting posthumous ennoblement and titling.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Jun memorialized requesting posthumous honors and an honorific posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎桂萼等言，儲立身輔政，有幹公議，因錄上兩京言官彈章。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Gui E and others said that in conducting himself and assisting government, Chu had offended public opinion; they therefore submitted the censorial memorials from both capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel Gui E and others said that in deportment and in office Chu had offended public opinion; they therefore forwarded the censorial memorials from both capitals.

sentences.zh: 帝念先朝舊臣，特贈太師，謚文康。

translations.literal: The emperor, remembering an old minister of the previous reign, specially posthumously ennobled him Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Wenkang.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of a veteran of the previous reign, the emperor specially posthumously ennobled him Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Wenkang.

sentences.zh: 先是，儲子次攄為錦衣百戶。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chu's son Cishu had been a centurion in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chu's son Cishu had served as a centurion in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 居家與富人楊端爭民田，端殺田主，次攄遂滅端家二百余人。

translations.literal: While at home he disputed civilian fields with the wealthy man Yang Duan; Duan killed the field's owner, and Cishu thereupon exterminated more than two hundred members of Duan's household.
translations.idiomatic: While living at home he disputed farmland with a wealthy man named Yang Duan; when Duan killed the landholder, Cishu exterminated more than two hundred members of Duan's household.

sentences.zh: 事發，武宗以儲故，僅發邊衛立功。

translations.literal: When the matter came to light, Wuzong, for Chu's sake, only sent him to earn merit on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair came to light, Wuzong, for Chu's sake, merely sent him to earn merit on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 後還職，累冒功至廣東都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Later restored to office, he repeatedly claimed merit by fraud until he reached vice commander of the regional military commission of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Later restored to office, he repeatedly claimed merit fraudulently until he reached vice commander of the Guangdong regional military commission.

sentences.zh: 蔣冕，字敬之，全州人。

translations.literal: Jiang Mian, styled Jingzhi, was a man of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Mian, styled Jingzhi, was from Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 兄昇，南京戶部尚書，以謹厚稱。

translations.literal: His elder brother Sheng was Minister of Revenue at Nanjing and was known for caution and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Sheng was Minister of Revenue at Nanjing and was known for caution and integrity.

sentences.zh: 冕舉成化二十三年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Mian passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-third year of Chenghua, was selected a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Mian passed the jinshi in Chenghua 23, was selected a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 弘治十三年，太子出閣，兼司經局校書。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Hongzhi the crown prince left the palace school; Mian also served as collator in the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 13 the crown prince left the palace school; he also served as collator in the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 正德中，累官吏部左侍郎，改掌詹事府，典誥敕，進禮部尚書，仍掌府事。

translations.literal: During Zhengde he rose step by step to Vice Minister of the Left in the Ministry of Personnel, was reassigned to head the Directorate of the Heir Apparent and supervise edicts of appointment, was promoted to Minister of Rites, and still administered the directorate.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he rose to Vice Minister of the Left in the Ministry of Personnel, was reassigned to head the Directorate of the Heir Apparent and draft edicts of appointment, was promoted Minister of Rites, and still headed the directorate.

sentences.zh: 冕清謹有器識，雅負時望。

translations.literal: Mian was clear-minded, cautious, and possessed judgment; he bore the esteem of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was clear-minded, cautious, and far-sighted, and enjoyed the esteem of his age.

sentences.zh: 十一年命兼文淵閣大學士，預機務。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was ordered to serve concurrently as Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Hall and to take part in confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was ordered to serve concurrently as Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Hall and to take part in state deliberations.

sentences.zh: 明年改武英殿，加太子太傅。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to the Wuying Hall and given the addendum Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was moved to the Wuying Hall and made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 近幸冒邊功，大行升賞，冕及梁儲亦蔭錦衣世千戶。

translations.literal: Favorites claimed frontier merit by fraud, and rewards of rank were bestowed on a large scale; Mian and Liang Chu also received hereditary commandancy of a thousand households in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Favorites claimed frontier merit fraudulently, and broad promotions followed; Mian and Liang Chu also received hereditary commandancy of a thousand households in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 兩人力辭，乃改文蔭。

translations.literal: The two strove to decline; they were then given hereditary civil appointments instead.
translations.idiomatic: Both men strenuously declined; they were then given hereditary civil appointments instead.

sentences.zh: 帝之以「威武大將軍」行邊也，冕時病在告，疏諫曰：「陛下自損威重，下同臣子，倘所過諸王以大將軍禮見，陛下何辭責之？

translations.literal: When the emperor went to the frontier as "valiant and martial grand general," Mian was at the time ill on leave; he memorialized in remonstrance, saying: "Your Majesty diminishes your own majesty and descends to the level of subjects; if the princes you pass treat you with the courtesy due a grand general, with what words will Your Majesty reprove them?
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to the frontier as "Valiant and Martial Grand General," Mian was then ill on leave; he memorialized in remonstrance, saying, "Your Majesty diminishes your own majesty and descends to the level of your subjects; if the princes you pass receive you with the courtesy due a grand general, with what words will Your Majesty reprove them?

sentences.zh: 曩睿皇帝北征，六軍官屬近三十萬，猶且陷於土木。

translations.literal: Once when the Sagacious Emperor campaigned north, the officers and men of the six armies numbered nearly three hundred thousand, yet they still fell into disaster at Tumu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chenghua emperor campaigned north, the officers and men of the six armies numbered nearly three hundred thousand, yet they still met disaster at Tumu.

sentences.zh: 今宿衛單弱，經行邊僥，寧不寒心？

translations.literal: Now the palace guard is meager and the journey passes the frontier by chance—can one not be chilled at heart?
translations.idiomatic: Now the palace guard is thin, and the route skirts the frontier by chance—should one not be chilled at heart?

sentences.zh: 請治左右引導者罪。」

translations.literal: I beg that the crimes of those at Your Majesty's side who guide you be punished."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that those at Your Majesty's side who guide this course be punished."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply was issued.
translations.idiomatic: No reply was issued.

sentences.zh: 十四年扈帝南征還，加少傅兼太子太傅、戶部尚書、謹身殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, having accompanied the emperor on the southern expedition and returned, he was given the addenda Junior Tutor and concurrent Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Revenue, and Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, having accompanied the emperor on the southern expedition and returned, he was made Junior Tutor and concurrent Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Revenue, and Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，與楊廷和協誅江彬。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, together with Yang Tinghe he cooperated in executing Jiang Bin.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, together with Yang Tinghe he cooperated in executing Jiang Bin.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，議定策功，加伯爵，固辭。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, deliberations on fixing the reward for settling the succession conferred an earldom; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took the throne, deliberations on rewards for settling the succession offered him an earldom; he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 改蔭錦衣世指揮，又辭。

translations.literal: It was changed to hereditary commandant in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard; he declined again.
translations.idiomatic: It was changed to hereditary commandant in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard; he declined again.

sentences.zh: 乃蔭五品文職，仍進一階。

translations.literal: He was then given a hereditary civil post of the fifth rank and still advanced one step.
translations.idiomatic: He was then given a hereditary fifth-rank civil post and still advanced one step in rank.

sentences.zh: 御史張鵬疏評大臣賢否，請罷冕。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Peng in a memorial evaluated whether the great ministers were worthy and requested that Mian be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Peng in a memorial judged whether the great ministers were worthy and asked that Mian be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 御史趙永亨詆石缶不可掌銓衡。

translations.literal: Censor Zhao Yongheng denounced Shi Fu as unfit to hold the power of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhao Yongheng denounced Shi Jiubao as unfit to hold the power of appointment.

sentences.zh: 冕、缶遂求去。

translations.literal: Mian and Shi thereupon asked to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Mian and Shi thereupon asked to leave.

sentences.zh: 朝議不平，諸給事、御史皆言其不可去。

translations.literal: Court opinion was indignant; the supervising secretaries and censors all said they should not be allowed to go.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion was indignant; the supervising secretaries and censors all said they should not be allowed to leave.

sentences.zh: 帝乃命鴻臚諭留，再下優詔，始起視事。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered the Court of State Ceremonial to instruct them to remain, and issued favorable edicts a second time before they resumed office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered the Court of State Ceremonial to instruct them to stay, and issued favorable edicts a second time before they resumed office.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年遣官織造江南，命冕草敕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing officials were dispatched to supervise weaving in Jiangnan; Mian was ordered to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 3 officials were dispatched to supervise weaving in Jiangnan; Mian was ordered to draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 冕以江南被災，具疏請止，帝不從，敕亦久不進。

translations.literal: Mian, because Jiangnan had suffered disaster, fully memorialized asking that it stop; the emperor did not agree, and the edict was long not submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Mian, because Jiangnan had suffered disaster, fully memorialized asking that it be halted; the emperor did not agree, and the edict was long withheld.

sentences.zh: 帝責其違慢，冕引罪而止。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached him for disobedience and dilatoriness; Mian took blame and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reproached him for disobedience and delay; Mian took blame and desisted.

sentences.zh: 「大禮」議起，冕固執為人後之說，與廷和等力爭之。

translations.literal: When the "great rites" dispute arose, Mian firmly held to the doctrine of being an heir to another line and strove against it together with Tinghe and the others.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Rites dispute arose, Mian firmly held to the doctrine of being an heir to another line and strove against the emperor's course together with Tinghe and the others.

sentences.zh: 帝始而婉諭，繼以譙讓，冕執議不回。

translations.literal: The emperor at first gave gentle instruction, then used reproach; Mian held to his view and did not turn back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at first gave gentle instruction, then turned to reproach; Mian held to his view and did not yield.

sentences.zh: 及廷和罷政，冕當國，帝愈欲尊崇所生。

translations.literal: When Tinghe left office, Mian held the chancellorship; the emperor all the more wished to honor his natural parents.
translations.idiomatic: When Tinghe left office, Mian headed the government; the emperor all the more wished to honor his natural parents.

sentences.zh: 逐禮部尚書汪俊以怵冕，而用席書代之，且召張璁、桂萼。

translations.literal: He drove out Minister of Rites Wang Jun to intimidate Mian, and used Xi Shu in his place, while also summoning Zhang Cong and Gui E.
translations.idiomatic: He drove out Minister of Rites Wang Jun to intimidate Mian, appointed Xi Shu in his place, and also summoned Zhang Cong and Gui E.

sentences.zh: 物情甚沸，冕乃抗疏極諫曰：「陛下嗣承丕基，固因倫序素定。

translations.literal: Public sentiment seethed; Mian then submitted an opposing memorial remonstrating to the utmost, saying: "Your Majesty has succeeded to the great foundation; this is indeed because the order of succession was long settled.
translations.idiomatic: Public sentiment seethed; Mian then submitted a forceful memorial remonstrating to the utmost, saying, "Your Majesty has succeeded to the great foundation; this is indeed because the order of succession was long settled.

sentences.zh: 然非聖母昭聖皇太后懿旨與武宗皇帝遺詔，則將無所受命。

translations.literal: Yet but for the august instruction of the Empress Dowager Zhaosheng and the testamentary edict of Emperor Wuzong, there would have been nowhere from which to receive the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet but for the august instruction of Empress Dowager Zhaosheng and the testamentary edict of Emperor Wuzong, there would have been no source from which to receive the mandate.

sentences.zh: 今既受命於武宗，自當為武宗之後。

translations.literal: Now that you have received the mandate from Wuzong, you should naturally be Wuzong's successor.
translations.idiomatic: Now that you have received the mandate from Wuzong, you should naturally be Wuzong's successor.

sentences.zh: 特兄弟之名不容紊，故但兄武宗，考孝宗，母昭聖。

translations.literal: Only the name of brother cannot be disordered; therefore you merely treat Wuzong as elder brother, Xiaozong as father in the rites, and Zhaosheng as mother.
translations.idiomatic: Only the name of brother cannot be disordered; therefore you merely treat Wuzong as elder brother, Xiaozong as father in the rites, and Zhaosheng as mother.

sentences.zh: 而於孝廟、武廟皆稱嗣皇帝，稱臣，稱御名，以示繼統承祀之義。

translations.literal: Yet toward the shrines of Xiaozong and Wuzong you are styled "successor emperor," call yourself subject, and use their taboo names—showing the meaning of inheriting the succession and continuing the sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yet toward the shrines of Xiaozong and Wuzong you are styled "successor emperor," call yourself subject, and use their taboo names—showing that you inherit the succession and continue the sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 今乃欲為本生父母立廟奉先殿側，臣雖至愚，斷斷知其不可。

translations.literal: Now you wish to erect temples for your natural parents beside the Hall of Imperial Ancestors; though I am utterly foolish, I am absolutely certain this cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Now you wish to erect temples for your natural parents beside the Hall of Imperial Ancestors; though I am utterly foolish, I am absolutely certain this cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 自古人君嗣位謂之承祧踐阼，皆指宗祀而言。

translations.literal: From antiquity, when a ruler succeeded to the throne it was called receiving the ancestral line and treading the dais—all referred to ancestral sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, when a ruler succeeded to the throne it was called receiving the ancestral line and treading the dais—all referred to ancestral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 《禮》為人後者惟大宗，以大宗尊之統也，亦主宗廟祭祀而言。

translations.literal: The Rites says that one who becomes another's heir serves only the great lineage, because the great lineage honors the succession—and this too concerns chiefly ancestral temples and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites says that one who becomes another's heir serves only the great lineage, because the great lineage honors the succession—and this too concerns chiefly ancestral temples and sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 自漢至今，未有為本生父母立廟大內者。

translations.literal: From Han until now, there has never been a case of erecting temples to one's natural parents within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: From Han until now, there has never been a case of erecting temples to one's natural parents within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝為叔祖昭帝後，止立所生父廟於葬所。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Han became heir to his uncle-grandfather Emperor Zhao and only erected a temple to his natural father at the burial place.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Han became heir to his uncle-grandfather Emperor Zhao and only erected a temple to his natural father at the burial place.

sentences.zh: 光武中興，本非承統平帝，而止立四親廟於章陵。

translations.literal: When Guangwu restored the dynasty, he had not in origin succeeded Emperor Ping, and only erected temples to four forebears at Zhangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangwu restored the dynasty, he had not in origin succeeded Emperor Ping, and only erected temples to four forebears at Zhangling.

sentences.zh: 宋英宗父濮安懿王，亦止即園立廟。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong of Song—his father was Prince Pu'an the Respectful and Majestic—and he too only erected a temple at the princely estate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong of Song—his father was Prince Pu'an the Respectful and Majestic—and he too only erected a temple at the princely estate.

sentences.zh: 陛下先年有旨，立廟安陸，與前代適同，得其當矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty in an earlier year issued an edict to erect a temple at Anlu, matching the former ages and hitting what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty in an earlier year issued an edict to erect a temple at Anlu, matching former ages and hitting what was fitting.

sentences.zh: 豈可既奉大宗之祀，又兼奉小宗之祀？

translations.literal: How can you already serve the sacrifices of the great lineage and also jointly serve those of the lesser lineage?
translations.idiomatic: How can you already serve the sacrifices of the great lineage and also jointly serve those of the lesser lineage?

sentences.zh: 夫情既重於所生，義必不專於所後，將孝、武二廟之靈安所托乎！

translations.literal: If feeling weighs heavier toward those who bore you, duty cannot be devoted solely to those to whom you are heir—where then will the spirits of the Xiaozong and Wuzong shrines find their resting place!
translations.idiomatic: If feeling weighs heavier toward those who bore you, duty cannot be devoted solely to those to whom you are heir—where then will the spirits of the Xiaozong and Wuzong shrines find their resting place!

sentences.zh: 竊恐獻帝之靈亦將不能安，雖聖心亦自不能安也。

translations.literal: I fear that the spirit of the late Prince of Xing will likewise be unable to rest, and even Your Majesty's own heart will be unable to rest.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that the spirit of the late Prince of Xing will likewise be unable to rest, and even Your Majesty's own heart will be unable to rest.

sentences.zh: 邇者復允汪俊之去，趣張璁、桂萼之來，人心益駭。

translations.literal: Recently you again allowed Wang Jun to leave and hastened the coming of Zhang Cong and Gui E; popular hearts grew still more alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Recently you again allowed Wang Jun to leave and hastened the coming of Zhang Cong and Gui E; popular hearts grew still more alarmed.

sentences.zh: 是日廷議建廟，天本晴明，忽變陰晦，至暮風雷大作。

translations.literal: On that day, when the court deliberated on erecting the temple, the sky had been clear and bright, then suddenly turned dark and gloomy; by evening wind and thunder broke out greatly.
translations.idiomatic: On that day, when the court deliberated on erecting the temple, the sky had been clear and bright, then suddenly turned dark and gloomy; by evening wind and thunder broke out greatly.

sentences.zh: 天意如此，陛下可不思變計哉？」

translations.literal: Heaven's intent is thus—can Your Majesty not consider changing your plan?"
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's intent is thus—can Your Majesty not consider changing your plan?"

sentences.zh: 因力求去。

translations.literal: He thereupon strove to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon strove to leave office.

sentences.zh: 帝得疏不悅，猶以大臣故，優詔答之。

translations.literal: The emperor received the memorial displeased, yet because he was a great minister, answered with a favorable edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the memorial displeased, yet because he was a great minister, answered with a favorable edict.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復請罷建廟之議，且乞休，疏中再以天變為言。

translations.literal: Before long he again asked that the plan to erect the temple be abandoned and begged to retire; in the memorial he again cited heaven's warnings.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he again asked that the plan to erect the temple be abandoned and begged to retire; in the memorial he again cited heaven's warnings.

sentences.zh: 帝益不悅，遂令馳傳歸，給月廩、歲夫如制。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still more displeased and ordered him to return home by courier transport, granting monthly stipends and annual corvée laborers according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still more displeased and ordered him to return home by courier transport, granting monthly stipends and annual corvée laborers as usual.

sentences.zh: 冕當正德之季，主昏政亂，持正不撓，有匡弼功。

translations.literal: In the late Zhengde period, when the ruler was benighted and government chaotic, Mian held firm without bending and had the merit of aiding and correcting.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Zhengde period, when the ruler was benighted and government chaotic, Mian held firm without bending and had the merit of aiding and correcting.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，朝政雖新，而上下捍格彌甚，冕守之不移。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign, though court affairs were renewed, obstruction between high and low grew still worse; Mian held his ground without shifting.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shizong's reign, though court affairs were renewed, obstruction between high and low grew still worse; Mian held his ground without shifting.

sentences.zh: 代廷和為首輔僅兩閱月，卒齟齬以去，論者謂有古大臣風。

translations.literal: Replacing Tinghe as chief minister for only two months, he finally left in discord; commentators said he had the bearing of the great ministers of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Replacing Tinghe as chief minister for only two months, he finally left in discord; commentators said he had the bearing of the great ministers of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 《明倫大典》成，落職閑住，久之卒。

translations.literal: When the Minglun Dadian was completed, he was stripped of office and lived in retirement; after a long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the Minglun Dadian was completed, he was stripped of office and lived in retirement; after a long time he died.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初復官，謚文定。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing his office was restored; he was given the posthumous title Wending.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longqing his office was restored; he was given the posthumous title Wending.

sentences.zh: 毛紀，字維之，掖縣人。

translations.literal: Mao Ji, styled Weizhi, was a man of Yexian.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Ji, styled Weizhi, was from Yexian.

sentences.zh: 成化末，舉鄉試第一，登進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: At the end of Chenghua he ranked first in the provincial examination, passed the jinshi, and was selected a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Chenghua he ranked first in the provincial examination, passed the jinshi, and was selected a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，授檢討，進修撰，充經筵講官，簡侍東宮講讀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi he was appointed proofreader, promoted to reviser, served as lecturer at the classics colloquium, and was chosen to attend the crown prince in the Eastern Palace as reader.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Hongzhi he was appointed proofreader, promoted to reviser, served as lecturer at the classics colloquium, and was chosen to attend the crown prince in the Eastern Palace as reader.

sentences.zh: 《會典》成，遷侍讀。

translations.literal: When the Huidian was completed, he was transferred to reader.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huidian was completed, he was transferred to reader.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，改左諭德。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, he was reassigned as Left Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong took the throne, he was reassigned as Left Mentor.

sentences.zh: 坐《會典》小誤，降侍讀。

translations.literal: For a minor error in the Huidian he was demoted to reader.
translations.idiomatic: For a minor error in the Huidian he was demoted to reader.

sentences.zh: 《孝宗實錄》成，擢侍講學士，為講官。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Xiaozong were completed, he was promoted to expositor and academician and served as lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of Xiaozong were completed, he was promoted to expositor and academician and served as lecturer.

sentences.zh: 正德五年進學士，遷戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengde he was advanced to academician and transferred to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 5 he was advanced to academician and transferred to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十年，由吏部左侍郎拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, from Vice Minister of the Left in the Ministry of Personnel he was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, from Vice Minister of the Left in the Ministry of Personnel he was appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 烏思藏入貢，其使言有活佛能前知禍福。

translations.literal: When U-Tsang sent tribute, its envoy said there was a living buddha who could foreknow fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: When U-Tsang sent tribute, its envoy said there was a living buddha who could foreknow fortune and misfortune.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中官劉允迎之。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched the palace eunuch Liu Yun to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched the palace eunuch Liu Yun to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 攜錦衣官百三十，衛卒及私仆隸數千人，芻糧、舟車費以百萬計。

translations.literal: He took with him one hundred thirty officers of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, several thousand guardsmen and private servants and retainers, with fodder, grain, and costs for boats and carts reckoned in the millions.
translations.idiomatic: He took with him one hundred thirty officers of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, several thousand guardsmen and private servants and retainers, with fodder, grain, and costs for boats and carts reckoned in the millions.

sentences.zh: 紀等上言：「自京師至烏思藏二萬餘里，公私煩費，不可勝言。

translations.literal: Ji and others memorialized, saying: "From the capital to U-Tsang is more than twenty thousand li; the trouble and expense to public and private cannot be fully stated.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and others memorialized, saying, "From the capital to U-Tsang is more than twenty thousand li; the trouble and expense to public and private cannot be fully stated.

sentences.zh: 且自四川雅州出境，過長河西行數月而後至。

translations.literal: Moreover, from leaving the border at Yazhou in Sichuan and traveling west of the Long River, several months pass before one arrives.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, from leaving the border at Yazhou in Sichuan and traveling west of the Long River, several months pass before one arrives.

sentences.zh: 無有郵驛、村市。

translations.literal: There are no postal stations or market villages.
translations.idiomatic: There are no postal stations or market villages.

sentences.zh: 一切資費，取辦四川。

translations.literal: All supplies are raised from Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: All supplies are raised from Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 四川連歲用兵，流賊甫平，蠻寇復起。

translations.literal: Sichuan had waged war year after year; bandits had only just been pacified and barbarian raiders rose again.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan had waged war year after year; bandits had only just been pacified and barbarian raiders rose again.

sentences.zh: 困竭之余，重加此累，恐生意外變。」

translations.literal: On top of exhaustion, to add this burden again may give rise to unforeseen changes."
translations.idiomatic: On top of exhaustion, to add this burden again may give rise to unforeseen changes."

sentences.zh: 疏再上，內閣梁儲、靳貴、楊一清皆切諫，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted again; Liang Chu, Jin Gui, and Yang Yiqing of the Grand Secretariat all remonstrated urgently; no reply was issued.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted again; Liang Chu, Jin Gui, and Yang Yiqing of the Grand Secretariat all remonstrated urgently; no reply was issued.

sentences.zh: 郊祀畢，請勤朝講，又以儲嗣未建，乞早定大計，亦不聽。

translations.literal: When the suburban sacrifice was completed, he asked that the emperor attend court diligently and lecture on the classics, and because the heir had not yet been established, begged that the great plan be settled early; this too was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When the suburban sacrifice was completed, he asked that the emperor attend court diligently and lecture on the classics, and because the heir had not yet been established, begged that the succession be settled early; this too was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 尋改理誥敕，掌詹事府。

translations.literal: Soon he was reassigned to manage patents and edicts and to head the Directorate of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was reassigned to manage patents and edicts and to head the Directorate of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十二年兼東閣大學士入預機務。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he served concurrently as Grand Secretary of the East Pavilion and entered confidential deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he served concurrently as Grand Secretary of the East Pavilion and entered confidential deliberations.

sentences.zh: 其秋加太子太保，改文淵閣。

translations.literal: That autumn he was given the addendum Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and transferred to the Wenyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and transferred to the Wenyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝南征，紀佐楊廷和居守。

translations.literal: When the emperor marched south, Ji assisted Yang Tinghe in holding the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched south, Ji assisted Yang Tinghe in holding the capital.

sentences.zh: 駕旋，晉少保、戶部尚書、武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, he was advanced to Junior Guardian, Minister of Revenue, and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from the southern tour, Ji was promoted to Junior Guardian, Minister of Revenue, and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，錄定策功，加伯爵，再疏辭免。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, his merit in settling the succession was recorded; he was enfeoffed as an earl and twice memorialized to decline.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took the throne, his role in securing the succession was rewarded with an earldom; he memorialized twice to decline.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，帝欲追尊興獻帝，閣臣執奏，忤旨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing, the emperor wished to posthumously honor the Xingxian Emperor; the grand secretaries memorialized firmly in opposition and offended the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiajing the emperor wished to posthumously honor his biological father; the grand secretaries held firm in memorial and defied his will.

sentences.zh: 三年，廷和、冕相繼去國。

translations.literal: In the third year, Tinghe and Mian left office one after another.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Yang Tinghe and Jiang Mian left office in succession.

sentences.zh: 紀為首輔，復執如初。

translations.literal: Ji became chief grand secretary and again held to his position as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Ji became chief grand secretary and again held his ground as before.

sentences.zh: 帝欲去本生之稱，紀與石缶合疏爭之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to remove the designation of biological parent; Ji and Shi Jiubao jointly memorialized in protest.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sought to drop the title of biological father, Ji and Shi Jiubao submitted a joint memorial of protest.

sentences.zh: 帝召見平臺，委曲諭意，紀終不從。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him for audience at Pingtai and explained his intent at length; Ji would not yield in the end.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him to Pingtai and explained his wishes at length, but Ji would not yield.

sentences.zh: 朝臣伏闕哭爭者，俱逮系，紀具疏乞原。

translations.literal: Court officials who knelt weeping at the palace gate in protest were all arrested and imprisoned; Ji submitted a full memorial asking that they be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who knelt weeping at the palace gate in protest were all arrested; Ji submitted a detailed memorial begging pardon for them.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，傳旨責紀要結朋奸，背君報私。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and issued an edict rebuking Ji for forming cliques and factions and betraying his sovereign to serve private ends.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the emperor issued an edict accusing Ji of forming factions, betraying his sovereign, and serving private ends.

sentences.zh: 紀乃上言曰：「曩蒙聖諭，國家政事商確可否，然後施行。

translations.literal: Ji thereupon submitted a statement, saying: "Previously I received Your Majesty's instruction that state affairs should be deliberated as to whether they were feasible or not, and only then carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Ji then memorialized, saying, "Your Majesty once instructed me that state affairs should be weighed for feasibility before they were enacted.

sentences.zh: 此誠內閣職業也，臣愚不能仰副明命。

translations.literal: This is indeed the duty of the Grand Secretariat; this foolish minister has been unable to live up to Your clear command.
translations.idiomatic: That is the Grand Secretariat's proper charge—and I, in my folly, have failed to meet Your clear command.

sentences.zh: 邇者大禮之議，平臺召對，司禮傳諭，不知其幾似乎商榷矣。

translations.literal: Recently, in the debate over the Great Rites, there were summons to audience at Pingtai and edicts transmitted by the Directorate of Ceremonial—how many times they seemed like consultation and deliberation!
translations.idiomatic: In the recent Great Rites debate there were audiences at Pingtai and edicts relayed by the Directorate of Ceremonial—how often they seemed like genuine consultation!

sentences.zh: 而皆斷自聖心，不蒙允納，何可否之有。

translations.literal: Yet all were decided by Your Majesty's own mind and were not accepted on our advice—what feasibility or unfeasibility was there?
translations.idiomatic: Yet every decision came from Your Majesty's own mind; none of our views was accepted—where was there any weighing of yes or no?

sentences.zh: 至於笞罰廷臣，動至數百，乃祖宗來所未有者，亦皆出自中旨，臣等不得與聞。

translations.literal: As for beating and punishing court officials, often to the number of several hundred—a thing without precedent since our founding ancestors—all likewise issued from the inner edict; we were not permitted to hear of them.
translations.idiomatic: As for flogging court officials by the hundreds—a thing unknown since the founding of the dynasty—all issued from inner edicts of which we were never informed.

sentences.zh: 宣召徒勤，捍格如故。

translations.literal: Edicts were summoned in vain; obstruction remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial summons came again and again, yet obstruction remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 慰留雖切，詰責隨加。

translations.literal: Though retention was urged with utmost earnestness, reproof and censure followed immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Though we were urged to stay with the utmost earnestness, reproof and censure followed at once.

sentences.zh: 臣雖有體國之心，不能自盡。

translations.literal: Though this minister has a heart that cherishes the state, I cannot exhaust myself in its service.
translations.idiomatic: Though I cherish the state in my heart, I can no longer give it my all.

sentences.zh: 宋司馬光告神宗曰：『陛下所以用臣，蓋察其狂直，庶有補於國家，若徒以祿位榮之而不取其言，是以官私非其人也。

translations.literal: Song dynasty's Sima Guang told Emperor Shenzong: 'Your Majesty employs your subject because you have discerned his bold straightforwardness, hoping he may be of some benefit to the state. If you merely honor him with salary and rank but do not take his words, you use the office for private ends and he is not the right man for it.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang of the Song told Emperor Shenzong: 'Your Majesty employs me because you discern my bold straightforwardness, hoping I may serve the state. If you honor me with salary and rank but heed none of my words, you treat office as a private reward and I am not the man for the post.

sentences.zh: 臣以祿位自榮，而不能救正，是徒盜竊名器以私其身也。』

translations.literal: If your subject takes pride in salary and rank but cannot rectify what is wrong, I am merely stealing title and office for my private gain.
translations.idiomatic: If I glory in salary and rank yet cannot set things right, I merely steal title and office for my private gain.

sentences.zh: 臣於陛下，敢舉以為告。

translations.literal: Toward Your Majesty, your subject dares offer this as his statement.
translations.idiomatic: Toward Your Majesty I dare offer the same counsel.

sentences.zh: 夫要結朋奸，背君報私，正臣平日所痛憤而深疾者。

translations.literal: Forming cliques and factions, betraying the sovereign to serve private ends—these are what upright ministers daily deplore and deeply hate.
translations.idiomatic: Forming factions and betraying one's sovereign for private ends—upright ministers deplore these every day and hate them to the bone.

sentences.zh: 有一於此，罪何止罷黜！

translations.literal: To have the slightest trace of them—what crime would stop short of dismissal!
translations.idiomatic: To harbor the slightest trace of them—what punishment would fall short of dismissal!

sentences.zh: 今陛下以之疑臣，尚可一日顏朝寧間哉。

translations.literal: Now that Your Majesty suspects your subject of them, how can I still show my face one day at court?
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Majesty suspects me of them, how can I still show my face at court for even a day?

sentences.zh: 乞賜骸骨歸鄉里，以全終始。

translations.literal: I beg to be granted my old bones and return to my home village, that beginning and end may both be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: I beg leave to take my old bones home and preserve my beginning and end in full.

sentences.zh: 尤望陛下法祖典學，任賢納諫，審是非，辨忠邪，以養和平之福。」

translations.literal: I especially hope Your Majesty will follow the ancestral models, study the classics, employ the worthy and accept remonstrance, examine what is right and what is wrong, distinguish loyalty from treachery, that the blessings of peace and harmony may be nurtured.
translations.idiomatic: Above all I hope Your Majesty will follow the ancestral models, study the classics, employ the worthy and heed remonstrance, judge right from wrong and loyalty from treachery, and so nurture the blessings of peace.

sentences.zh: 帝銜紀亢直，允其去，馳驛給夫廩如故事。

translations.literal: The emperor resented Ji's obstinate straightforwardness but granted his departure, sending courier transport and granaries according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor resented Ji's stubborn rectitude but granted his request, providing courier transport and grain stipends as usual.

sentences.zh: 紀有學識，居官廉靜簡重。

translations.literal: Ji had learning and erudition; in office he was incorrupt, quiet, and dignified.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was learned and erudite; in office he was incorruptible, reserved, and grave.

sentences.zh: 與廷和、冕正色立朝，並為縉紳所倚賴。

translations.literal: Together with Tinghe and Mian he stood at court with stern rectitude, and all were relied upon by the officialdom.
translations.idiomatic: With Tinghe and Mian he stood at court in stern rectitude, and the whole official class relied on them.

sentences.zh: 其代冕亦僅三月。

translations.literal: His replacement of Mian likewise lasted only three months.
translations.idiomatic: His tenure replacing Mian likewise lasted only three months.

sentences.zh: 後《明倫大典》成，追論奪官。

translations.literal: Later, when the Minglun Dadian was completed, his office was posthumously revoked in retrospective judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Minglun Dadian was completed, his office was retrospectively stripped in the settling of accounts.

sentences.zh: 久之，廷和、冕皆淪喪，紀以恩詔敘復，帝亦且忘之。

translations.literal: After a long time, when Tinghe and Mian had both died, Ji was restored to office by grace edict; the emperor too had nearly forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward, when Tinghe and Mian had both died, Ji was restored by grace edict; the emperor had nearly forgotten him.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，年八十，撫按以聞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, at age eighty, the surveillance officials reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, at eighty, the provincial surveillance officials reported his condition.

sentences.zh: 詔遣官存問，再賜夫廩。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched an official to inquire after his health and again bestowed courier transport and grain.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent an official to inquire after him and again granted courier transport and grain.

sentences.zh: 又三年卒。

translations.literal: Three years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太保，謚文簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian and given the posthumous title Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the posthumous title Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 子渠，進士，太仆卿。

translations.literal: His son Qu was a jinshi and became Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qu, a jinshi, rose to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 石缶，字邦彥，槁城人。

translations.literal: Shi Jiubao, styled Bangyan, was a man of Gaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jiubao, styled Bangyan, was from Gaocheng.

sentences.zh: 父玉，山東按察使。

translations.literal: His father Yu was regional inspector of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu had served as regional inspector of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 缶與兄玠同舉成化末年進士，改庶吉士，授檢討，數謝病居家。

translations.literal: Jiubao and his elder brother Jie both passed the jinshi at the end of Chenghua, were made Hanlin bachelors, appointed proofreaders, and repeatedly asked leave to remain at home on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Jiubao and his elder brother Jie both passed the jinshi at the end of Chenghua, entered the Hanlin as bachelors, were appointed proofreaders, and repeatedly took leave to convalesce at home.

sentences.zh: 孝宗末，始進修撰。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiaozong's reign he was finally promoted to reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the end of Xiaozong's reign was he promoted to reviser.

sentences.zh: 正德改元，擢南京侍讀學士。

translations.literal: When Zhengde began, he was promoted to Reader of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengde began he was made Reader in the Nanjing Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 歷兩京祭酒，遷南京吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He served as libationer of both capitals and was transferred to Vice Minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served as libationer in both capitals and was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 召改禮部，進左侍郎。

translations.literal: Summoned and transferred to the Ministry of Rites, he was advanced to Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the Ministry of Rites, he was promoted to Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 武宗始遊宣府，缶上疏力諫，不報。

translations.literal: When Wuzong first toured Xuanfu, Jiubao memorialized forcefully in remonstrance but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong first toured Xuanfu, Jiubao memorialized in forceful remonstrance but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 改掌翰林院事。

translations.literal: He was reassigned to direct affairs of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to direct the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 廷臣諫南巡，禍將不測，缶疏救之。

translations.literal: When court officials remonstrated against the southern tour and disaster seemed imminent, Jiubao memorialized to save them.
translations.idiomatic: When court officials remonstrated against the southern tour and calamity seemed near, Jiubao memorialized to save them.

sentences.zh: 十六年拜禮部尚書，掌詹事府。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Minister of Rites and director of the Directorate of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was made Minister of Rites and director of the Directorate of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，代王瓊為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, he replaced Wang Qiong as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took the throne he replaced Wang Qiong as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 自群小竊柄，銓政混濁。

translations.literal: Since petty men had seized power, appointments were turbid and corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men had seized power, and appointments had grown murky and corrupt.

sentences.zh: 缶剛方，謝請托，諸犯清議者多見黜，時望大孚，而內閣楊廷和有所不悅。

translations.literal: Jiubao was upright and stern; he refused requests and recommendations; many who had offended pure discussion were dismissed, and public expectation was greatly fulfilled—yet Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe was somewhat displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Jiubao was upright and unyielding; he refused patronage and petitions, and many who had offended upright opinion were dismissed—public esteem swelled, though Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe was somewhat displeased.

sentences.zh: 甫二月，復改掌詹事府，典誥敕。

translations.literal: After barely two months he was again reassigned to direct the Directorate of the Heir Apparent and patents and edicts.
translations.idiomatic: After barely two months he was again reassigned to the Directorate of the Heir Apparent to manage patents and edicts.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年遣祀闕里及東嶽。

translations.literal: In Jiajing year 1 he was dispatched to sacrifice at Qufu and Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 1 he was dispatched to perform sacrifices at Qufu and Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 事竣還家，屢乞致仕。

translations.literal: When the task was completed he returned home and repeatedly begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed he returned home and repeatedly begged to retire.

sentences.zh: 言官以缶望重，交章請留，乃起赴官。

translations.literal: Censorial officials, because Jiubao's standing was weighty, memorialized one after another asking that he remain; he was then raised and took office.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jiubao's standing was weighty, censorial officials memorialized one after another asking that he stay; he was then recalled to office.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，詔以吏部尚書兼文淵閣大學士入參機務。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of year 3, an edict appointed him Minister of Personnel concurrent with Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Hall to participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 3 an edict made him Minister of Personnel concurrent with Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Hall to join in confidential deliberations.

sentences.zh: 帝欲以奉先殿側別建一室祀獻帝，缶抗疏言其非禮。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to build a separate chamber beside the Hall of Imperial Ancestors to sacrifice to the Presentation Emperor; Jiubao remonstrated forcefully that it was contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to build a separate chamber beside the Hall of Imperial Ancestors to sacrifice to his biological father; Jiubao remonstrated forcefully that it violated ritual.

sentences.zh: 及廷臣伏闕泣爭，缶與毛紀助之。

translations.literal: When court officials knelt weeping at the gate in protest, Jiubao and Mao Ji assisted them.
translations.idiomatic: When court officials knelt weeping at the palace gate in protest, Jiubao and Mao Ji supported them.

sentences.zh: 無何，「大禮」議定，紀去位。

translations.literal: Before long the Great Rites were settled and Ji left office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Great Rites were settled and Ji left office.

sentences.zh: 缶復諫曰：「大禮一事已奉宸斷，無可言矣。

translations.literal: Jiubao remonstrated again, saying: "The matter of the Great Rites has already received Your Majesty's decision; there is nothing more to say.
translations.idiomatic: Jiubao remonstrated again, saying, "The Great Rites have already received Your Majesty's final decision; nothing more remains to be said.

sentences.zh: 但臣反復思之，終有不安於心者。

translations.literal: Yet your subject, pondering it again and again, still has something that cannot rest easy in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet pondering it again and again, I still cannot set my heart at ease.

sentences.zh: 心所不安而不以言，言恐觸忤而不敢盡，則陛下將焉用臣，臣亦何以仰報君父哉？

translations.literal: What the heart cannot rest easy with yet does not speak—if one fears that speech may offend and therefore dare not speak fully—then how will Your Majesty employ your subject, and how will your subject repay his sovereign and father?
translations.idiomatic: What the heart cannot rest easy with yet goes unspoken—if one fears offense and therefore dares not speak fully—how will Your Majesty employ me, and how shall I repay my sovereign and father?

sentences.zh: 夫孝宗皇帝與昭聖皇太后，乃陛下骨肉至親也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong and Empress Dowager Zhaosheng are bone and flesh, your closest kin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong and Empress Dowager Zhaosheng are your flesh and blood, your closest kin.

sentences.zh: 今使疏賤讒佞小人輒行離間，但知希合取寵，不復為陛下體察。

translations.literal: Now base, mean, slanderous petty men at once set themselves to sow division; they know only how to curry favor by compliance and no longer consider things from Your Majesty's perspective.
translations.idiomatic: Now base slanderers and flatterers at once sow division; they know only how to curry favor and no longer weigh matters for Your Majesty's sake.

sentences.zh: 茲孟冬時享在邇，陛下登獻對越，如親見之，寧不少動於中乎？

translations.literal: Now the winter seasonal sacrifice draws near; when Your Majesty ascends to present offerings and faces the spirits across, as if seeing them in person—will you not be somewhat moved within?
translations.idiomatic: The winter seasonal sacrifice draws near; when Your Majesty ascends to present offerings and faces the spirits across, as if seeing them in person—will you not be moved within?

sentences.zh: 夫事亡如事存。

translations.literal: To serve the dead as one serves the living.
translations.idiomatic: To serve the dead as one serves the living.

sentences.zh: 陛下承列聖之統，以總百神，臨萬方，焉得不加慎重，顧聽細人之說，幹不易之典哉？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty inherits the line of the successive sages, to preside over the hundred spirits and face the ten thousand regions—how can you fail to add caution? yet you heed the words of petty men and overturn unchanging canonical rites!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty inherits the line of the sage emperors, presiding over the hundred spirits and facing the ten thousand realms—how can you fail to be cautious? Yet you heed petty men's words and overturn unchanging canonical rites!

sentences.zh: 帝得奏不悅，戒勿復言。

translations.literal: The emperor received the memorial unhappily and warned him not to speak again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the memorial unhappily and warned him not to speak again.

sentences.zh: 明年建世廟於太廟東。

translations.literal: The next year the Shizong shrine was built east of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Shizong shrine was built east of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 帝欲從何淵言，毀神宮監，伐林木，以通輦道。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to follow He Yuan's proposal to destroy the Directorate of Divine Music, fell timber, and open an imperial processional way.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to follow He Yuan's proposal to demolish the Directorate of Divine Music, fell timber, and open an imperial processional route.

sentences.zh: 給事中韓楷，御史楊秦、葉忠等交諫，忤旨奪俸。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Han Kai and Censors Yang Qin, Ye Zhong, and others remonstrated in succession; they offended the will and had their salaries seized.
