translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Han Kai and Censors Yang Qin, Ye Zhong, and others remonstrated in turn; they offended the throne and had their salaries seized.

sentences.zh: 給事中衛道繼言之，貶秩調外。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wei Dao spoke next and was demoted and transferred outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Wei Dao spoke next and was demoted and transferred outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 缶復抗章，極言不可，弗聽。

translations.literal: Jiubao again submitted a forceful memorial saying it could not be done; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jiubao again submitted a forceful memorial saying it must not be done; the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及世廟成，帝欲奉章聖皇太后謁見，張璁、桂萼力主之。

translations.literal: When the Shizong shrine was completed the emperor wished to lead Empress Dowager Zhangsheng to pay a visit; Zhang Cong and Gui E strongly advocated it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizong shrine was completed the emperor wished to lead Empress Dowager Zhangsheng to visit it; Zhang Cong and Gui E strongly urged it.

sentences.zh: 禮官劉龍等爭不得，諸輔臣以為言，帝不報，趣具儀。

translations.literal: Ritual officials Liu Long and others protested without success; the chief ministers spoke on it but the emperor gave no response and urged that the ceremonies be prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials Liu Long and others protested in vain; the chief ministers spoke as well, but the emperor gave no reply and ordered the ceremonies prepared.

sentences.zh: 缶乃上疏曰：「陛下欲奉皇太后謁見世廟，臣竊以為從令固孝，而孝有大於從令者。

translations.literal: Jiubao then submitted a memorial, saying: "Your Majesty wishes to lead the empress dowager to visit the Shizong shrine; your subject ventures to think that to comply with the command is indeed filial, yet there is a filial piety greater than mere compliance.
translations.idiomatic: Jiubao then memorialized, saying, "Your Majesty wishes to lead the empress dowager to visit the Shizong shrine; I venture to think that obeying the command is filial, yet there is a filial piety greater than mere obedience.

sentences.zh: 臣誠不敢阿諛以誤君上。

translations.literal: Your subject truly dares not flatter and deceive to mislead his sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: I truly dare not flatter and mislead my sovereign.

sentences.zh: 竊惟祖宗家法，后妃已入宮，未有無故復出者。

translations.literal: I reflect on the ancestral household law: once an empress or consort has entered the palace, none has ever left without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the ancestral household law: once an empress or consort has entered the palace, none has ever left without cause.

sentences.zh: 且太廟尊嚴，非時享祫祭，雖天子亦不輕入，況后妃乎？

translations.literal: Moreover the Imperial Ancestral Temple is august; except at the seasonal sacrifices and joint offerings, even the Son of Heaven does not lightly enter—how much more an empress or consort?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Imperial Ancestral Temple is august; except at seasonal sacrifices and joint offerings, even the Son of Heaven does not enter lightly—how much less an empress or consort?

sentences.zh: 璁輩所引廟見之禮，今奉先殿是也。

translations.literal: The temple-audience rite that Zhang and his faction cite—today that is the Hall of Imperial Ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: The temple-audience rite Zhang and his faction cite is today performed at the Hall of Imperial Ancestors.

sentences.zh: 聖祖神宗行之百五十年，已為定制，中間納后納妃不知凡幾，未有敢議及者，何至今日忽倡此議？

translations.literal: The sacred ancestors Shenzu and Shenzong practiced it for a hundred fifty years and it has become fixed custom; in between, how many empresses and consorts entered the palace—none dared raise this discussion. Why suddenly advocate this today?
translations.idiomatic: The Holy Ancestor and Shenzong practiced it for a hundred fifty years until it became fixed custom; empresses and consorts entered the palace beyond counting, yet none dared raise this question—why suddenly advocate it today?

sentences.zh: 彼容悅佞臣豈有忠愛之實，而陛下乃欲聽之乎？

translations.literal: Those flattering, fawning wicked ministers—do they have any real loyalty and love? And yet Your Majesty would heed them?
translations.idiomatic: Those fawning wicked ministers—do they harbor any real loyalty? And yet Your Majesty would heed them?

sentences.zh: 且陰陽有定位，不可侵越。

translations.literal: Moreover yin and yang have fixed positions and must not be transgressed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover yin and yang have fixed positions and must not be transgressed.

sentences.zh: 陛下為天地百神之主，致母后無故出入太廟街門，是坤行乾事，陰侵陽位，不可之大者也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is lord of the hundred spirits of heaven and earth; to have the empress dowager leave the palace gate of the Imperial Temple without cause—to let the kun perform the qian role, yin encroaching on yang's position—is the greatest of what cannot be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is lord of the hundred spirits of heaven and earth; to let the empress dowager pass without cause through the Imperial Temple's gate—to let yin perform yang's office, the feminine encroaching on the masculine—is the greatest of violations.

sentences.zh: 臣豈不知君命當承，第恐上累聖德，是以不敢順旨曲從，以成君父之過，負覆載之德也。」

translations.literal: Your subject knows well that the sovereign's command ought to be obeyed; I only fear it will weigh upon your sacred virtue—therefore I dare not comply with bent intent and follow crookedly, completing a fault of sovereign and father and failing the debt of heaven and earth that covers and bears us.
translations.idiomatic: I know well that a subject must obey his sovereign; I only fear this will stain Your sacred virtue—therefore I dare not bend to the command and thereby complete a fault of sovereign and father, failing the debt heaven and earth bear toward us.

sentences.zh: 奏入，帝大慍。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor was greatly enraged.

sentences.zh: 珤為人清介端亮，孜孜奉國。

translations.literal: Jiubao was pure, upright, and bright in conduct, tireless in serving the state.
translations.idiomatic: Jiubao was pure, upright, and luminous in character, tireless in serving the state.

sentences.zh: 數以力行王道，清心省事，辨忠邪，敦寬大，毋急近效為帝言。

translations.literal: He often spoke to the emperor of practicing the kingly way, purifying the heart and reducing affairs, distinguishing loyalty from treachery, promoting magnanimity, and not seeking quick near-term results.
translations.idiomatic: He often urged the emperor to practice the kingly way, purify the heart and lighten affairs, distinguish loyalty from treachery, cherish magnanimity, and not chase quick results.

sentences.zh: 帝見為迂闊，弗善也。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded him as pedantic and impractical and took no liking to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found him pedantic and impractical and took no liking to him.

sentences.zh: 議「大禮」時，帝欲援以自助，而缶據禮爭，持論堅確，失帝意，璁、萼輩亦不悅。

translations.literal: During the debate on the Great Rites the emperor wished to enlist his support, but Jiubao argued by ritual and held his position firmly, losing imperial favor; Zhang Cong, Gui E, and their faction were also displeased.
translations.idiomatic: During the Great Rites controversy the emperor wished to enlist his support, but Jiubao argued from ritual and held firm, losing imperial favor; Zhang Cong, Gui E, and their faction were displeased as well.

sentences.zh: 璁、萼朝夕謀輔政，攻擊費宏無虛日，以缶行高，不能有所加。

translations.literal: Zhang and Gui plotted day and night to share in governing, attacking Fei Hong every day without respite; because Jiubao's conduct was loftier, they could not add anything against him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang and Gui plotted day and night for a share in power, attacking Fei Hong daily without respite; because Jiubao's conduct was too lofty, they could find no hold on him.

sentences.zh: 至明年春，奸人王邦奇訐楊廷和，誣缶及宏為奸黨，兩人遂乞歸。

translations.literal: By the spring of the following year, the wicked man Wang Bangqi denounced Yang Tinghe and falsely charged Jiubao and Hong as a faction of traitors; the two men thereupon begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: By the spring of the following year the villain Wang Bangqi denounced Yang Tinghe and falsely charged Jiubao and Hong as traitors in league; the two men thereupon begged to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝許宏馳驛，而責缶歸怨朝廷，失大臣誼，一切恩典皆不予。

translations.literal: The emperor granted Hong courier transport but rebuked Jiubao for harboring resentment toward the court and failing the duty of a great minister; no grace or favor whatever was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted Hong courier transport but rebuked Jiubao for nursing resentment against the court and failing the duty of a great minister; no grace whatever was granted.

sentences.zh: 歸，裝襆被車一輛而已。

translations.literal: On returning home, one cart of bedding was his entire baggage.
translations.idiomatic: On returning home, a single cart of bedding was his entire baggage.

sentences.zh: 都人嘆異，謂自來宰臣去國，無若缶者。

translations.literal: The capital's people sighed in wonder, saying that since ministers left office, none had been like Jiubao.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the capital marveled, saying that in living memory no departing minister had been like Jiubao.

sentences.zh: 自缶及楊廷和、蔣冕、毛紀以強諫罷政，迄嘉靖季，密勿大臣無進逆耳之言者矣。

translations.literal: From Jiubao and Yang Tinghe, Jiang Mian, and Mao Ji being dismissed for forceful remonstrance until the end of Jiajing, confidential ministers dared advance no words that offended the ear.
translations.idiomatic: From the dismissal of Jiubao, Yang Tinghe, Jiang Mian, and Mao Ji for forceful remonstrance until the end of Jiajing, no confidential minister dared speak words that offended the ear.

sentences.zh: 珤加官，自太子太保至少保。

translations.literal: Jiubao's addendum of offices ran from Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent to Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Jiubao's accumulated offices ran from Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent to Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 七年冬卒，謚文隱。

translations.literal: In the winter of year 7 he died and was given the posthumous title Wenyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year 7 he died and was given the posthumous title Wenyin.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，改謚文介。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing the posthumous title was changed to Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longqing the posthumous title was changed to Wenjie.

sentences.zh: 玠，字邦秀。

translations.literal: Jie, styled Bangxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Jie, styled Bangxiu.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，由汜水知縣召為御史。

translations.literal: During Hongzhi he was summoned from magistrate of Sishui to censor.
translations.idiomatic: During Hongzhi he was summoned from his post as magistrate of Sishui to serve as censor.

sentences.zh: 出核大同軍儲，按甘肅及陜西，所條上邊務，悉中機宜，為都御史戴珊所委寄。

translations.literal: He went out to audit Datong military stores, inspected Gansu and Shaanxi, and in the frontier matters he memorialized upward, all hit the opportune points; he was entrusted by Censor-in-Chief Dai Shan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to audit Datong military stores and to inspect Gansu and Shaanxi; every item he submitted on frontier affairs was entirely to the point, and Censor-in-Chief Dai Shan placed great trust in him.

sentences.zh: 嘗因災異劾南京刑部尚書翟瑄以下二十七人。

translations.literal: Once, on account of portents and disasters, he impeached Nanjing Minister of Justice Zhai Xuan and twenty-seven others below him.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he used portents and natural disasters as grounds to impeach Nanjing Minister of Justice Zhai Xuan and twenty-six officials beneath him.

sentences.zh: 正德中，累官右副都御史，巡撫大同，召拜兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign he rose through successive posts to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, grand coordinator of Datong, and was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he rose step by step to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Datong, then was summoned to the capital as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 海西部長數犯邊，泰寧三衛與別部相攻，久缺貢市，遣玠以左侍郎兼僉都御史往遼東巡視。

translations.literal: Haixi tribal chiefs repeatedly violated the border; the three guards of Taining and other divisions attacked one another; tribute markets had long been suspended—Jie was dispatched as Left Vice Minister concurrently serving as Censor-in-Chief to go to Liaodong and inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Haixi chiefs raided the frontier repeatedly; the three Taining guards and other tribes were fighting one another; tribute trade had long been cut off—so Jie was sent to Liaodong as Left Vice Minister with the concurrent title of Censor-in-Chief to conduct an inspection.

sentences.zh: 出關撫諭，皆受約束。

translations.literal: Going beyond the pass he pacified and instructed them; all accepted restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Once he went beyond the pass to pacify and instruct them, all submitted to his authority.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，璽書嘉勞，召還。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, sent an imperial letter under seal to praise and reward him, and summoned him back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, sent him an imperial letter under seal commending his service, and recalled him to court.

sentences.zh: 左都御史陸完遷，廷推代者，三上悉不用，最後推玠，乃以為右都御史掌院事。

translations.literal: Left Censor-in-Chief Lu Wan was transferred; the court nominated a successor—three nominations were all rejected; at last Jie was nominated, and he was then made Right Censor-in-Chief to direct the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: When Left Censor-in-Chief Lu Wan was transferred, the court put forward successors three times without success; Jie was finally nominated and appointed Right Censor-in-Chief to head the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 御史李隱劾玠夤緣，不報。

translations.literal: Censor Li Yin impeached Jie for currying favor; no reply was issued.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Yin accused Jie of winning office through backdoor influence, but the memorial went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 十年拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Zhengde he was appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 中官史大鎮雲南，請獨領銀場務。

translations.literal: The eunuch Shi Da, stationed in Yunnan, requested exclusive control of the silver-mining administration.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Shi Da, who held command in Yunnan, asked to take sole charge of the silver-mining administration.

sentences.zh: 杜甫鎮湖廣，請借鹽船稅銀為進貢資。

translations.literal: Du Fu, commanding Huguang, requested to borrow salt-transport tax silver as funds for tribute offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fu, military commissioner of Huguang, asked to divert salt-transport tax silver to pay for tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 劉德守涼州，請帶食茶六百引。

translations.literal: Liu De, defending Liangzhou, requested to carry six hundred yin of tribute tea for personal use.
translations.idiomatic: Liu De, defending Liangzhou, asked permission to take six hundred yin of tribute tea for his own use.

sentences.zh: 玠皆執不可。

translations.literal: Jie in every case held firm that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Jie refused every request.

sentences.zh: 西僧闡教王請船三百艘販載食鹽，玠極言其害。

translations.literal: The western monk, the Dharma-King Who Spreads the Teaching, requested three hundred ships to trade and transport table salt; Jie spoke at length of the harm.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan Dharma-King Who Spreads the Teaching asked for three hundred ships to carry and sell table salt; Jie memorialized at length on the damage this would do.

sentences.zh: 帝初出居庸，玠切諫。

translations.literal: When the emperor first went out through Juyong, Jie remonstrated urgently.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first set out through Juyong Pass, Jie remonstrated in the strongest terms.

sentences.zh: 及在宣府，需銀百萬兩，玠持不可。

translations.literal: When he was at Xuanfu and needed one million taels of silver, Jie held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was at Xuanfu and demanded a million taels of silver, Jie insisted the demand could not be met.

sentences.zh: 帝弗從，乃進其半。

translations.literal: The emperor would not follow him; only half was then advanced.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed him, and only half the sum was finally supplied.

sentences.zh: 王瓊欲以哈密事害彭澤，玠獨廷譽之。

translations.literal: Wang Qiong wished to use the Hami affair to harm Peng Ze; Jie alone praised him in court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiong sought to use the Hami affair to ruin Peng Ze, but Jie alone spoke in Peng's defense at court.

sentences.zh: 奸民欲牟鹽利者，賄朱寧為請，玠不可，連章執奏。

translations.literal: Wicked commoners who wished to profit from salt bribed Zhu Ning to plead for them; Jie would not agree and submitted memorial after memorial insisting on refusal.
translations.idiomatic: Unscrupulous men hoping to profit from the salt trade bribed Zhu Ning to plead their case; Jie refused and submitted repeated memorials insisting on denial.

sentences.zh: 廷臣諫南巡跪闕下，諸大臣莫敢言，玠獨論救。

translations.literal: Court officials remonstrated against the southern tour by kneeling at the palace gate; the senior ministers did not dare speak; Jie alone argued to save them.
translations.idiomatic: When court officials knelt at the palace gate to remonstrate against the southern tour, the chief ministers dared not speak; Jie alone pleaded for their lives.

sentences.zh: 群小激帝怒，嚴旨責令自陳，遂引疾去。

translations.literal: Petty men incited the emperor's anger; a stern edict ordered him to explain himself, and he thereupon cited illness and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Petty favorites inflamed the emperor's wrath; a stern edict ordered Jie to explain himself, whereupon he pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 賜敕馳傳給廩隸如故事。

translations.literal: He was granted an imperial edict, express relay transport, and stipends and retainers according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted an imperial edict, express relay transport, and stipends and household retainers as usual for a retiring minister.

sentences.zh: 家居二年卒，贈太子少傅。

translations.literal: After two years at home he died and was posthumously given the title Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Two years after returning home he died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 玠有操行，居官亦持正。

translations.literal: Jie had integrity of conduct and in office also held to what was right.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was a man of moral integrity and remained upright in office.

sentences.zh: 其為都御史時，胡世寧論寧王，玠與李士實請罪世寧，以是為人所譏。

translations.literal: When he was Censor-in-Chief, Hu Shining memorialized against the Prince of Ning; Jie and Li Shishi asked that Hu be punished—for this he was ridiculed by others.
translations.idiomatic: While he was Censor-in-Chief, Hu Shining denounced the Prince of Ning; Jie and Li Shishi called for Hu to be punished—a move for which he was widely criticized.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：武宗之季，君德日荒，嬖幸盤結左右。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: In the late years of Emperor Wuzong, the ruler's virtue daily declined, and favorites clustered thickly at his left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: In the closing years of Emperor Wuzong the throne's virtue daily declined, and favorites clustered around the emperor.

sentences.zh: 廷和為相，雖無能改於其德，然流賊熾而無土崩之虞，宗藩叛而無瓦解之患者，固賴廟堂有經濟之遠略也。

translations.literal: Tinghe as chief minister, though unable to reform the ruler's virtue, yet with roving bandits raging there was no fear of the realm collapsing, and with enfeoffed princes in rebellion there was no danger of disintegration—this indeed relied on the court's far-reaching plans for statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tinghe as chief minister could not reform the emperor's conduct, yet while bandits raged the state did not crumble, and while enfeoffed princes rebelled it did not fall apart—this owed much to far-sighted statecraft at the top of government.

sentences.zh: 至其誅大奸，決大策，扶危定傾，功在社稷，即周勃、韓琦殆無以過。

translations.literal: As for his execution of the great traitor, his resolution of great policies, his support of the endangered and stabilization of the tottering—the merit was to the altars of state; even Zhou Bo and Han Qi could scarcely surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: In executing the great traitor, settling great policies, and shoring up a tottering dynasty, his service to the state was such that even Zhou Bo and Han Qi could hardly have done better.

sentences.zh: 儲雖蒙物議，而大節無玷。

translations.literal: Chu, though he incurred public criticism, in great principle was unstained.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chu, though he drew criticism, was without stain on the great points of conduct.

sentences.zh: 蔣冕、毛紀、石缶，清忠鯁亮，皆卓然有古大臣風。

translations.literal: Jiang Mian, Mao Ji, and Shi Jiubao—pure, loyal, and uprightly outspoken—all outstandingly bore the air of great ministers of old.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Mian, Mao Ji, and Shi Jiubao were pure, loyal, and outspoken—each unmistakably a minister in the ancient mold.

sentences.zh: 自時厥後，政府日以權勢相傾。

translations.literal: From that time onward, the government daily tilted toward mutual rivalry in power.
translations.idiomatic: From that time on, the government grew ever more a contest of power against power.

sentences.zh: 或脂韋淟涊，持祿自固。

translations.literal: Some were oily and obsequious, holding office to secure their salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Some were slick and servile, clinging to office merely to preserve their stipends.

sentences.zh: 求如諸人，豈可多得哉。

translations.literal: To seek men like these—how could they be found in any great number?
translations.idiomatic: To find men like these again—how could one hope for many?
